As a leading technology innovator, Qualcomm pushes the boundaries of what's possible to enable next-generation experiences and drives digital transformation to help create a smarter, connected future for all. As a Qualcomm GPU Engineer, you may architect, design, implement, verify, and/or optimize the performance and power of GPU cores. jobs.title: Software Engineering Manager - Strategic Data Solutions.
jobs.desc:
Summary
Apple's Strategic Data Solutions (SDS) team is seeking a hands-on, self-motivated Software Engineering Manager to deliver cutting-edge analytical solutions with enhanced user experience. Our mission is Enterprise Decision Automation, protecting Apple and our customers from fraud, waste, and abuse. Your contributions will be pivotal to our success.
Do you thrive on solving complex challenges with direct, meaningful impact? Are you passionate about building tools and systems that enable data analysis over petabytes of data?
Do you want to work alongside talented Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, Software Engineers, Program Managers, and Apple business partners? If so, we'd love to have you on our team!
Description
With the expansive data we have, our job is to build meaningful tools and solutions that empower our internal partners and drive fraud prevention across Apple. The Solutions SWE team is a global, cross-LOB (line-of-business) engineering team focused on four core areas: efficiency solutions, internal tooling, operational excellence, and direct LOB support.
As the Engineering Manager for Solutions SWE, you will directly lead and grow a team of 5-6 Software Engineers based in Cork, Ireland (EMEA), while contributing to the broader functional roadmap across regions. You will balance hands-on technical leadership with people management, developing talent, and partnering with fraud investigators, analysts, engineers, product managers, and business partners to ship solutions that solve real business problems.
Responsibilities
Directly managing, coaching, and growing the engineering team in Cork, including hiring, performance management, and career development
Contributing to the functional and technical roadmap for Solutions SWE, in partnership with regional counterparts
Partnering with fraud investigators, analysts, product managers, and business partners to gather requirements, set priorities, and deliver outcomes
Ensuring the team ships reliable, scalable production software and automation that reduces manual work across operations, analytics, and engineering
Owning delivery end-to-end from planning and development through deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement
Coordinating across time zones and regional teams to keep a distributed organization aligned and effective
Partnering with the broader SWE organization to align on technical patterns and grow the engineering craft of the team
Minimum Qualifications
3+ years leading software engineers, either as a people manager or as a technical lead who directed the day-to-day work of a team of at least 3 engineers
Hands-on experience writing and shipping production software in Python, Java, or a comparable language, with code contributions in the last 2 years
Experience owning delivery end to end, from planning and development through deployment, monitoring and iteration
Experience working with non-engineering partners (for example product, operations, analysts or business stakeholders) to gather requirements and agree priorities
Experience working with teams spread across multiple locations or time zones
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with or exposure to machine learning, useful for partnering with MLEs
Track record of quickly getting productive with new AI/LLM tooling.
Hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure and container orchestration (AWS, Kubernetes)
Experience with data pipeline, warehousing, and/or observability tooling (Airflow, Snowflake, Splunk, Superset)
Expertise in real-time systems, modern architecture, and data processing at scale
Experience building systems for fraud prevention or similarly challenging problems
Educational background in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent practical experience

jobs.title: Christmas Customer Assistant
jobs.desc:
Please note, this role is located in IRELAND
Ready to make someone's day this Christmas? Join Boots as a Seasonal Customer Assistant and be part of something special.
The festive season at Boots is one of the busiest and most exciting times of the year, and we're looking for enthusiastic people to help create brilliant experiences for our customers when it matters most.
About The Opportunity
As a Seasonal Customer Assistant, you'll be at the heart of the action, helping customers find the perfect gift, discover great offers and get what they need for the celebrations ahead.
You'll be the friendly face customers turn to for advice and support, creating feel-good moments that make a real difference and keep them coming back all year round.
This is an important role where you'll help deliver a great experience for our customers. It's also a fast-paced and active role where priorities can change quickly throughout the day.
You won't just be helping customers on the shop floor. You'll also support deliveries, replenish stock, and help keep the store looking its best.
Working in store is a real team effort, so you'll need to be flexible and ready to step into different areas to keep things running smoothly. You'll feel good knowing you're playing your part and enjoy a strong sense of teamwork and fun as everyone pulls together during our busiest season.
If you enjoy helping people, staying busy and being part of a supportive team, this could be the role for you.
This is a temporary role, with the potential for longer-term opportunities depending on local availability.
You Will
What you'll be doing
Welcome customers, understand their needs and help them find the right products, gifts, services and offers.
Create memorable customer experiences through friendly, personalised service.
Help customers complete purchases using tills and self-checkouts.
Replenish stock and keep shelves full
Support deliveries and help organise stock in the stockroom.
Keep the store and shopping areas look their best.
Work across different areas of the store and support your team wherever help is needed.
What You'll Need To Have (our Must-haves)
Available to work Bank Holidays including Black Friday week and weekend, Cyber Monday, Christmas Eve, St Stephen's Day and New Year's Day.
Customer-focused — enjoys talking to people and helping customers have a great experience.
Team player — supports others and cares about team success.
Operations ready — comfortable balancing customer service with stock, fulfilment and shop floor tasks.
Proactive attitude — sees what needs doing and takes ownership.
Resilient — stays positive and focused during busy periods.
Energy and stamina — keeps energy high throughout long, active shifts.
Confident asking questions — asks for help when needed to get things right.
Comfortable with technology — learns new systems and confidently uses handheld devices, tills and self-checkouts.
It would be great if you also have
Previous experience in a retail or customer-facing environment.
Familiarity with Boots products and services.
Where your brilliance can take you
You’ll receive industry-recognised training and build valuable experience along the way. You may go on to explore more in Retail, Pharmacy, Beauty or Opticians, or ultimately progress into management. There are plenty of paths to follow for you to become brilliant with Boots —you can read some of our
colleagues stories here.
Rewards designed for you
Discretionary Christmas bonus
Generous employee discount (After 1 month’s service)
Access to our One Hub discount platform
There’s lots more in our benefits and discounts, MyBoosts – there to give you that little lift in your everyday. Find out more at
boots.jobs/ireland
Exclusions may apply; eligible roles only. Please note that any salary estimates provided on third-party sites are not endorsed by Boots and may not be accurate.

At Boots, we're proud to be an equal opportunity employer, creating a place where everyone feels welcome, supported, and free to be themselves. We believe that when our people feel valued and included, they thrive, so we're committed to creating a brilliant Boots for our people so they can make a difference for our customers and colleagues every time.

jobs.title: Façade Supervisor
jobs.desc:
Role Overview
The Façade Supervisor will lead the onsite construction of the Brick façade. The role will act as the primary contact and coordinator for the Bricklayers, Brickwork accessories installers, Window installers, scaffolders, fire barrier installers etc. The Façade Supervisor will be working closely with the Site Manager, Site Engineers and Project Manager. The Façade Supervisor will drive Brickwork quality and output on the project.
Key Responsibilities
Lead, supervise and coordinate bricklaying operatives and subcontractors to ensure works are completed safely, efficiently and in line with project programmes.
Plan daily and weekly activities, allocating labour, materials and equipment to maximise productivity and meet construction milestones.
Review drawings, specifications and construction details to ensure masonry works are delivered in accordance with design requirements.
Monitor workmanship standards and carry out regular quality inspections to ensure all brickwork, blockwork and masonry installations meet company and client expectations.
Coordinate material deliveries, storage and usage on site, minimising waste and ensuring sufficient resources are available to maintain progress.
Liaise closely with Site Managers, Engineers, Quantity Surveyors and other trade supervisors to coordinate works and resolve site issues.
Identify and address technical, logistical and labour-related challenges, implementing practical solutions to maintain programme objectives.
Ensure compliance with project-specific method statements, risk assessments and company health & safety policies, promoting a strong safety culture across all masonry activities.
Monitor progress against programme requirements and provide regular updates to Site Management, highlighting risks, delays and mitigation measures.
Maintain accurate site records including labour returns, progress reports, quality inspections and site instructions.
Assist with the training, mentoring and development of bricklaying operatives and apprentices, promoting best practice and continuous improvement.
Support project handover activities, ensuring snagging items are completed promptly and all masonry works are delivered to the required standards.
Requirements
Proven experience as a Bricklaying Foreman, Lead Bricklayer or similar supervisory role on residential, commercial, industrial or large-scale construction projects.
Extensive practical knowledge of brickwork, blockwork, masonry construction techniques and associated construction processes.
Strong ability to interpret construction drawings, specifications and technical details.
Demonstrated experience managing site labour, subcontractors and material resources to achieve programme targets.
Sound understanding of quality control procedures and workmanship standards within masonry construction.
Excellent leadership and communication skills, with the ability to motivate teams and build strong working relationships with site management, clients and subcontractors.
Strong organisational and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced construction environment.
Good understanding of health & safety legislation, safe systems of work and site compliance requirements.
Competent in the use of Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook; experience using digital site reporting and project management systems is desirable.
Relevant trade qualification in Bricklaying or Masonry Construction. SSSTS, SMSTS or equivalent site supervisory qualification would be advantageous.
Full driving licence and willingness to travel between project locations as required.
Rewards & Benefits
A competitive and attractive rewards package, including pension scheme, professional subscription support and additional company benefits.
Opportunities for professional development, training and long-term career progression within the company.

At Walls Construction, we believe diversity strengthens our business and inclusion fosters innovation. We are committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels respected, supported, and valued.

jobs.title: Sr. Analyst, Payroll AMR
jobs.desc:
Logitech is the Sweet Spot for people who want their actions to have a positive global impact while having the flexibility to do it in their own way.
Global Payroll Senior Analyst
Position Summary:
Department: Controllership Finance – Global Payroll Team
Location: Cork, Ireland - On site 2 days a week
Contract Type: Full Time / Permanent
Region Coverage: AMR
About the Role:
As an integral member of Logitech Finance, you will work in a fast-paced, dynamic Global Payroll team processing payrolls across the Americas region — covering the United States, Canada, and Latin America. You will play a key role in ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely payroll delivery, while helping to drive continuous improvement across our payroll operations.
Your Contribution:
Be Yourself. Be Open. Stay Hungry and Humble. Collaborate. Challenge. Decide and Do.
In this role you will:
Ensure the accurate and timely processing of Logitech’s end-to-end payroll for the AMR region (USA, Canada, and LATAM).
Collaborate with payroll partners to collect and validate all payroll inputs, including salaries, bonuses, benefits, allowances, and deductions. Conduct rigorous pre- and post-payroll reconciliations to eliminate anomalies or duplicate records before finalization.
Ensure the accurate and timely completion of payroll fiscal close procedures, including journal entries and balance sheet reconciliations. Work with the broader Finance team to identify and resolve payroll accounting exceptions.
Understand the full payroll cycle through to GL bookings and present meaningful flux analysis to stakeholders.
Stay current on and ensure strict compliance with federal, state/provincial, and local payroll regulations, tax laws, social security, and benefits requirements across all AMR jurisdictions.
Ensure compliance with payroll internal controls, maintaining robust documentation and proactively identifying and remediating any control gaps or weaknesses. Assist in facilitating internal and external audit engagements.
Partner with key stakeholders including People Services, HRIS, Compensation & Benefits, Stock Admin, and Finance to troubleshoot issues and work collaboratively to develop optimum processes and service delivery.
Drive the payroll Global Finance Transformation roadmap, focusing on eliminating manual workflows and implementing scalable, automated payroll solutions.
Collaborate with internal and external partners to drive automation and enhance service delivery.
Your Skills & Experience:
Beyond core technical payroll knowledge, we are seeking an innovative, highly data-literate payroll professional who actively identifies opportunities to leverage modern tools, AI, and emerging technologies to automate workflows and transform end-to-end payroll operations.
For consideration, you must bring the following skills, experience and behaviours to our team:
Experience: 3+ years of proven experience in a senior analyst payroll role, specifically working with Americas payroll (US required; Canada and LATAM experience is a major plus).
Education & Certification: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field—or an equivalent payroll certification.
Regulatory Compliance: Solid understanding of US/Canadian payroll taxes, statutory deductions, and labour regulations.
Hands-on experience processing payroll and running reports in Workday and/or Dayforce (Ceridian).
Spreadsheet Skills: Advanced proficiency in MS Excel and Google Sheets (must be comfortable using Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and managing large data sets).
Familiarity with how HRIS data flows into downstream payroll and Finance/GL systems.
Strong ability to perform pre- and post-payroll reconciliations, investigate gross-to-net variances, and flag data errors before finalization.
Experience supporting month-end close procedures, including preparing journal entries and assisting Finance/FP&A teams with cost analysis.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills to partner effectively across HR, Finance, and external vendors.
Ability to stay organized and solve problems independently in a fast-paced, global team environment.
Customer service focus with the ability and sound judgment to handle highly sensitive information.
Process improvement mindset: have a passion for reengineering payroll processes in implementing a first-class payroll service.
Strong interest in applying emerging technologies—such as AI, ML, and RPA—to re-engineer enterprise payroll workflows, eliminate manual touchpoints, and unlock value-added insights for workforce planning.
About Logitech
With a fast-moving, innovative culture and a strong balance sheet, Logitech is a world leader in products that connect people to the digital experiences they care most about. Video conferencing, remote work, content creation, and gaming are long-term secular trends driving our business — and today all of them have accelerated, making Logitech more relevant to customers than ever.
Logitech is the sweet spot for people who are passionate about products, making a mark, and having fun doing it. We're small and flexible enough for every person to take initiative — and big enough for those actions to have a global impact.
Across Logitech we empower collaboration and foster play. We help teams collaborate/learn from anywhere, without compromising on productivity or continuity so it should be no surprise that most of our jobs are open to work from home from most locations. Our hybrid work model allows some employees to work remotely while others work on-premises. Within this structure, you may have teams or departments split between working remotely and working in-house.
Logitech is an amazing place to work because it is full of authentic people who are inclusive by nature as well as by design. Being a global company, we value our diversity and celebrate all our differences. Don’t meet every single requirement? Not a problem. If you feel you are the right candidate for the opportunity, we strongly recommend that you apply. We want to meet you!
We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits packages and working environments that are designed to be flexible and help you to care for yourself and your loved ones, now and in the future. We believe that good health means more than getting medical care when you need it. Logitech supports a culture that encourages individuals to achieve good physical, financial, emotional, intellectual and social wellbeing so we all can create, achieve and enjoy more and support our families. We can’t wait to tell you more about them being that there are too many to list here and they vary based on location.

jobs.desc:
The Opportunity
THE OPPORTUNITY
This is an opportunity to join Stantec’s growing water sector team in Ireland, where you will contribute to the delivery of critical infrastructure that supports communities, protects the environment, and addresses the challenges of climate change. As a Civil Engineer, you will work on a diverse range of water and wastewater projects, from concept and feasibility through to detailed design and construction support, gaining exposure across the full project lifecycle.
You will be part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment, working alongside experts in engineering, environmental science, and planning to deliver integrated and sustainable solutions. The role offers the chance to build your technical expertise in areas such as network design, treatment processes, and asset management, while also developing your project management and client-facing skills
About The Role
As a Civil Engineer in Stantec’s water team, you will support the delivery of water and wastewater projects across all stages, from concept to construction. You will contribute to technical design work, including drawings, calculations, and specifications, while assisting with reports and contract documentation.
Working within a multidisciplinary team, you will collaborate with engineers, environmental specialists, and project managers, gaining broad project experience and exposure to clients and stakeholders. This role offers a strong platform to develop your technical skills and grow your career within Ireland’s water sector.
YOUR IMPACT
In this role, you will contribute to the delivery of essential water and wastewater infrastructure that supports communities, public health, and environmental protection across Ireland. Your work will help ensure reliable water services, improve network performance, and enhance resilience to climate change.
By applying sound engineering principles and attention to detail, you will support the development of practical, efficient, and sustainable design solutions. Your input will help projects meet regulatory requirements, reduce environmental impact, and deliver long-term value for clients and stakeholders.
Through collaboration with multidisciplinary teams, you will play a part in driving high-quality project outcomes, strengthening client relationships, and supporting the continued growth and reputation of Stantec in Ireland’s water sector.
About You
You are a qualified Civil Engineer with a strong technical foundation and proven experience in water network design. You bring a practical, solutions-focused mindset and are comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary team.
You Will Demonstrate
A minimum Level 8 degree in Engineering (or a related discipline)
Strong post-graduate experience in water network design
Solid professional and technical knowledge, with the ability to apply engineering principles effectively
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage with colleagues and clients
WHY JOIN US
We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025. =
We do what is right: Industry leading training and development as well as paid for professional subscriptions. A professional progression plan, supporting you to become chartered.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment to assist with the growth of your career.
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard!

Whether you’re starting out on your engineering career or are looking for a fresh challenge, Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, is a great career move.
Based in Dublin, Galway, Castlebar and Cork, we are actively recruiting for team players with experience in any of the following areas – water and wastewater treatment process and network design, integrated network management, structural design, site development, road and bridge engineering, project management and administration.
You’ll be working for a dynamic company with an excellent reputation in the industry.
Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, offers a great working environment amongst friendly professionals with an emphasis on teamwork. It’s a company where your ideas and opinions will be valued and your efforts recognised and rewarded.

jobs.title: Design Manager (Design & Build)
jobs.desc:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.
Your impact
You will help turn some of the UK & Ireland's most important water and wastewater plans into safe, buildable and effective infrastructure.
Working across multidisciplinary programmes, you will bring engineering disciplines, construction teams and client stakeholders together around clear, coordinated design decisions. You will help identify risks early, improve buildability and make sure commissioning, operational performance and whole-life value are considered throughout the design process.
This is a role for an experienced engineering professional who understands how complex designs move from development into delivery. You will coordinate technical interfaces, manage design information and help project teams resolve issues before they affect construction, programme or cost.
You will work closely with project managers, technical specialists and construction teams, providing design management support and giving clients confidence that designs are coordinated, assured and ready for delivery.
Your contribution will go beyond managing drawings and schedules. You will challenge assumptions, support better ways of working and help teams make practical decisions that improve safety, value and long-term performance.
About The Opportunity
The UK water sector is entering a significant period of investment, creating the opportunity to improve the resilience, capacity and environmental performance of critical infrastructure.
As a Design Manager, you will coordinate multidisciplinary detailed design activities across water and wastewater projects and programmes. You will work with civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, process and construction teams to produce integrated, buildable designs that support successful delivery, commissioning and operation.
You will take day-to-day responsibility for defined design packages or project workstreams, helping manage scope, programme, technical interfaces, assurance requirements and design change. Working alongside senior design managers, project managers and discipline leads, you will track progress, coordinate inputs and help resolve technical or delivery issues.
You will also work closely with construction and commissioning teams to make sure buildability, sequencing, access, safety and operational requirements are reflected in the design. Where opportunities exist, you will support the use of standardised solutions, digital tools and lessons learned to improve design efficiency and consistency.
Depending on the size and complexity of the programme, you may coordinate a small design team or manage several technical packages within a larger multidisciplinary delivery environment. You will provide clear direction and constructive support, but you will not be expected to carry the same practice leadership, business development or people-management responsibilities as a Senior Design Manager.
This is a great opportunity to join a growing water practice and take on greater responsibility across complex infrastructure programmes. Success will mean improving design coordination, identifying risk early and helping multidisciplinary teams produce engineering solutions that work in design, construction and operation.
This role can be based out of several locations across our major UK & Ireland offices
Here's what you'll need
We would be delighted to hear from and speak to candidates with a progressive mix of the following
Experience coordinating the design or engineering delivery of water, wastewater or comparable infrastructure projects within a consultancy, contractor, delivery partner or asset-owner environment.
Evidence of managing defined design packages or project workstreams, including design scope, programme, technical interfaces, deliverables, assurance activities and change.
Practical understanding of how engineering design interacts with construction, commissioning, operations and maintenance
Working knowledge of Design & Build contracts and CDM requirements, helping teams identify, record and manage design risk.
Experience working within NEC3 or NEC4 delivery environments, including an understanding of change control, early warnings and the relationship between design decisions, programme and cost.
We offer
Competitive salary We offer compensation that reflects your skills and experience
Flexible Work Arrangements Benefit from hybrid, part-time, and flexible working hours, patterns, and locations
Robust Pension Contributions We offer enhanced pension contributions up to 10% to secure your future
Comprehensive Health Coverage Single medical cover and Digital GP service, with options to add your partner and family
Family Planning Support Access to fertility healthcare and family planning services
Enhanced Parental Leave Enjoy enhanced parental leave pay and free membership to employee assistance and parental programs
Life assurance at 4x your salary
Wellbeing Hub Free access to wellbeing apps like Calm and Daily Burn
Professional Development We cover professional membership fees and provide continuous professional development (CPD) opportunities
Community Engagement Participate in charity matched-funding, paid volunteering time, and charitable donations

Ensure all plant utilities and facilities operate safely, reliably, and efficiently to support site production requirements.
Manage and optimise site utility systems including boilers, chillers, air compressors, refrigeration systems, HVAC, and associated infrastructure.
Troubleshoot complex equipment failures and identify long-term solutions to improve reliability and performance.

Lead root cause investigations using methodologies such as Fault Tree Analysis, Fishbone Diagrams, FMEA, and 8D.

Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Sustainability Engineering, Marine Engineering, or a related discipline.
Minimum 5-7 years' experience in maintenance, utilities, facilities, energy management, or a related engineering environment.
Strong technical knowledge of utility systems such as boilers, chillers, refrigeration systems, compressed air systems, and associated plant infrastructure.
Experience developing maintenance strategies, asset management plans, and capital replacement programmes.
Experience managing engineering projects from concept through implementation.
Strong troubleshooting and root cause analysis capabilities.
Knowledge of maintenance management systems, preferably SAP PM.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

The Role:
The Brand Protection Manager is responsible for safeguarding the company’s brand integrity across European markets by identifying, investigating, and mitigating risks related to unauthorized distribution, parallel trade, non-compliant SKUs, and abuse of commercial programs. This role works cross-functionally with Legal, Sales, Supply Chain, and external partners to enforce brand standards and protect revenue, reputation, and customer trust.

Parallel Trade Monitoring & Control
Monitor and analyze parallel trade activities across EU markets.
Identify unauthorized distribution channels and gray market activities.

Collaborate with regional teams to enforce territorial distribution agreements.
Non-Compliant SKU Management

Collaborate with Finance, Trade Compliance and Legal to address confirmed cases and mitigate financial impact.

Analyze sales data, distribution flows, and market trends to identify anomalies, risks, and opportunities.
Develop dashboards and KPIs to monitor brand protection, compliance risks, and program integrity.
Provide regular reports and actionable insights to senior management to support informed, compliant decision-making.
External Partner Management
Manage relationships with third-party investigators, brand protection agencies, and legal counsel.
Oversee vendor performance and ensure alignment with company policies and EU legal frameworks.
Ensure all external activities are conducted in compliance with applicable laws and internal standards.

For consideration, you must bring the following minimum skills and behaviours to our team:
5+ years of experience in brand protection, compliance, anti-counterfeiting, or distribution control.
Strong understanding of EU trade regulations, parallel trade dynamics, and compliance requirements.
Experience with investigations, audits, and enforcement actions.
Analytical mindset with proficiency in data analysis tools (Excel, BI tools).

We believe that good health means more than getting medical care when you need it. Logitech supports a culture that encourages individuals to achieve good physical, financial, emotional, intellectual and social wellbeing so we all can create, achieve and enjoy more and support our families. We can’t wait to tell you more about them being that there are too many to list here and they vary based on location.

jobs.title: Kepak Operational Rotational Graduate Programme 2027 - Ireland
jobs.desc:
We are seeking to recruit for the 2027 Operational Rotational Graduate Programme at either our Kepak Longford or Kepak Cork site.
Our Operations Graduates will embark on an intensive learning journey within our business, gaining a comprehensive understanding of the entire production process from procurement to sales. This role is designed to develop future leaders in the meat industry, with a strong emphasis on learning the end-to-end process, understanding the value of each step, and mastering the operations that drive our business. The ultimate goal is for the graduate to be able to articulate the entire process, and to demonstrate this knowledge through presentations and hands-on experience.
Key Responsibilities
End-to-End Process Learning: Rotate through various operational departments, to gain hands-on experience of every role and a deep understanding of each stage of the production process
Presentation and Reporting: At the end of each rotation, present the acquired knowledge and insights to demonstrate an understanding of the operations
Operational Involvement: Actively participate on the factory floor, learning each work station and the processes involved producing our products
People Management: Develop skills in managing diverse teams, understanding the dynamics of a labour-intensive industry, and learning how to effectively communicate and lead in a multicultural environment
Continuous Improvement: Engage in key projects such as data gathering, writing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), process improvement initiatives, and customer-specific projects to contribute to the overall efficiency of operations
Key Competencies
Numerical Proficiency: Strong aptitude for working with numbers, crucial for understanding the yield, value, and financial aspects of meat processing
Work Ethic: A strong work ethic is essential. Demonstrating a background in consistent part-time work during studies is an advantage
Process Management: Ability to motivate teams in a labour-intensive environment, with a focus on maintaining calm and effective communication in high-pressure situations
Problem-Solving: Strong problem-solving skills, particularly in high-pressure environments where quick thinking and decision-making are required
Teamwork: Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a team, whether through sports, work, or academic projects
Other Role Information
Location: Full-time on-site at our Kepak Longford site, with the possibility of travel to other locations for specialised learning
Progression: The program will involve 90% factory floor experience and 10% office-based work initially, with a gradual increase in office responsibilities as you progress
Assessment: You will be assessed through presentations and practical demonstrations of your understanding at each stage of the process. You will also have a Learner Journey to support your progress, this states key competencies that we want you to develop through your programme
Our Operational Graduate programme allows dynamic, motivated, hardworking, and passionate Graduates an opportunity start their career with one of the top 100 brands in the UK. The programme lasts 2 years.
What can you expect?
To be fully immersed into our Culture from day 1, working alongside industry experts and Kepak leaders
An opportunity to gain in depth knowledge and skill in various Operational departments across the business, with a rotation plan tailored to your development
Gain real, hands on experience in our manufacturing areas, to understand how our teams come together to create our brilliant products
The opportunity to work with the commercial side of the business, through shorter placements, to gain insight into the whole of the business
Gain an in depth understanding of our brands and products, and how they are made, and our relationships with customers and consumers
To learn key aspects of our business, whilst you develop your skills and knowledge
The opportunity to develop personally and professionally through exposure to key projects, tasks and development activities that challenge you, all supported by a detailed learner journey and training plan
A dedicated mentor and development program to support you both on the programme and into a role that best fits your skill
Start date:
September 6th 2027
Starting Salary
- €33,500 with an up to €1,500 increase at the start of Year 2 to €35,000
Role Location
- Kepak Longford, Co. Longford, Ireland or Kepak Watergrasshill, Cork, Ireland depending on candidate location.
Read more about our programme and hear from some of our Graduates
:
https://www.kepak.com/careers/graduates/
Requirements
Who are we looking for?
We are looking for hardworking and ambitious Graduates, who want to learn and grow in a challenging and fast paced environment, by performing real roles as part of your rotations.
You must be mobile and willing to travel throughout the programme to undertake development activities at any of our sites in the UK and Ireland.
We will consider undergraduates from all disciplines and backgrounds.
We will be looking for alignment with our Core Values:
Responsibility
- Ability to work on your own initiative and take accountability for your actions
Ambition
- You will have the willingness and confidence to challenge yourself to be the best you can be and be driven to succeed
Passion for Food
- this is at the heart of everything we do, you must be passionate about every aspect of our industry
Teamwork
- ability to build positive relationships quickly with people from all cultures and career stages is pivotal

When you join us, you’ll be part of a global team harnessing the power of scientific testing and data-driven insights to build a healthier future.

jobs.title: Research Assistant- AI assisted design ICs capture BioSignals
jobs.desc:
Research Assistant- AI assisted design ICs capture BioSignals
About Tyndall
Tyndall National Institute is an international leader in semiconductors, photonics and deep-tech research and innovation. As a leading collaborative European research institute, Tyndall is a key actor and hosting partner in the delivery of the ‘Chips for Europe Initiative’ (EU Chips Act).
Tyndall is Ireland’s leading research and innovation organisation and it is the national focal point for excellence in deep-tech research, development and graduate training at the convergence of nanotechnology, microelectronics, photonics, electronics and AI. Tyndall is recognised as an international research leader in semiconductor, chip and digital technologies, particularly as applied to the fields of Information & Communications, Health & Life Sciences, Agritech & Food Security, Energy and Climate Mitigation, emerging fields such as quantum, and novel computing paradigms.
The Institute’s key objective is to see frontier research activities having a significant impact on economic development and societal challenges in Ireland, Europe and beyond. Central to Tyndall’s mission is delivering economic impact through research excellence in partnership with industry and academia. With an annual turnover of more than €50m, the Institute has a community of over 600 researchers, engineers, support staff, postgraduate students, interns and industry researchers-in-residence.
With significant committed Irish government support, Tyndall will grow to be 1,000 people by 2030, with approximately 750 researchers, including 250 PhD students. A new 17,000 m2 research building is under development adjacent to the Cork headquarters and there are developing plans to expand Tyndall’s existing Dublin research labs and to establish other research sites within Ireland.
Tyndall’s expansion is also supported by recent national and EU funding wins for significant (M€10’s) additional research equipment across a range of areas such as semiconductor processing, microscopy, quantum technologies, heterogeneous integration, ultra-high speed optical communications and RF through THz characterisation.
About the Team
The integrated circuits group at Tyndall National Institute consist of a large team of researchers in silicon chip design, at various stages of their careers; from Masters researcher through to Principal Researcher. All are creating advanced, innovative and high impact Integrated Circuit technologies, which will shape our future lives. Excellent research is being carried out in areas such as Analog Precision Circuits, RF and Millimeter-wave Communications circuits, Cryogenic CMOS and Integrated Power Systems.
About the Role
Design of a Wide-bandwidth (RF) low noise amplifier
The objective of this position is to apply AI assisted circuit design methods to design amplifiers and Analog to Digital converter blocks. The circuit blocks will be used to build a system to capture Bio electrical signals like ECG and EMG.
Key Duties & Responsibilities
The candidate is expected to be creative, self-motivated, and should help create an efficientl and friendly atmosphere within the Integrated Circuits Group and beyond to all teams at Tyndall.
Propose AI assisted design methods to Simulate, Design and Layout analogue circuits either using Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools from industry standard vendors like Cadence or custom or open source tools
With guidance from the senior Tyndall design team propose innovative circuits to meet the bio sensing application
Perform schematic design, simulation and analysis across PVT corners and relevant operating conditions
Work with guidance from experienced layout engineers to ensure effective layout implementation of analogue circuits, including matching, parasitics, shielding, grounding, isolation and other layout considerations
Prepare presentations and reports
Support project management
Participate in Education and Public Engagement activities, as required
Ensure compliance with Tyndall’s Quality Management Systems, Health and Safety standards, and other regulations
Carry out any additional duties as may reasonably be required within the general scope and level of the post
Essential Criteria
The successful candidate must have:
a MEng or equivalent experience (e.g. BEng + 2 years’ experience) in a relevant discipline such as electrical/electronic engineering, physics or related relevant discipline;
experience in designing integrated circuits in the areas of Analogue, Mixed-Signal or RF circuit design;
experience with designing and simulating integrated circuits using tools such as Cadence/Siemens-Mentor/Synoposys;
strong communication skills, as evidenced by prior experience such as working with/in industry, scientific paper writing, conference presentation and report writing
Knowledge of analogue circuits e.g. amplifiers or comparators
Knowledge of AI algorithms
Desirable Criteria
Knowledge of Integrated circuit layout
Good mathematical ability and knowledge of statistics
Experience programming with Python
What We Offer
Apart from offering a position in a highly successful and positive research environment, with a collaborative ethos full of diverse competencies to boost your career, we offer the following:
Impactful Work: Opportunities to contribute to ground-breaking research and innovation that shape Ireland’s economy and the society at large.
Continuous Learning: Strong support for formal training, further study and professional development.
Interdisciplinary Environment: Where academia, industry, and innovation intersect - supported by cutting-edge infrastructure and expert knowledge.
Blended Working: Flexibility to work remotely and on-site, where the role allows.
Comprehensive Benefits: Access to UCC pension, long-term illness benefit, life assurance, and more.
Generous Leave: Competitive annual leave entitlements.
Equity & Inclusion: Athena Swan Bronze award holder, with ongoing initiatives led by a dedicated People and Culture team to ensure equity for all.
Core Values: A culture grounded in Ambition, Collaboration, Diversity, Excellence, and Integrity.
Entrepreneurial Spirit: A proactive, innovation-driven environment that welcomes entrepreneurial and creative thinkers, including those with start-up experience.
Supportive Onboarding: Structured induction and mentoring to help new hires integrate and thrive.
Vibrant Culture: A collaborative, people-first workplace with a strong sense of community.
Terms of Employment
Contract Category: Full-Time
Contract Type: Fixed Term
The duration of the project is 7 months in the first instance, although this may be extended for an additional year pending funding and performance.
Appointment may be made on the Research Assistant Salary Scale i.e. €34,129- €44,311 per annum. Placement on appointment will be in accordance with public sector pay policy.
For further information, please contact to Dr. Daniel O' Hare.
Closing date of applications is 1pm, 16th October 2026.
Application Instructions
Please make sure to attach an up to date CV/Resume AND a brief motivation letter outlining how you meet the ‘Essential Criteria’ for this role.
Please note that Garda vetting and/or an international police clearance check may form part of the selection process.
At this time, Tyndall National Institute does not require the assistance of recruitment agencies.
Tyndall National Institute at University College, Cork is an Equal Opportunities Employer

jobs.title: Renewable Energy Analyst (Graduate)
jobs.desc:
Renewable Energy Analyst (Graduate)
Location:
Cork (hybrid)
Salary:
€45,000 - €55,000, depending on experience
Type:
Full-time, permanent
About us
We are a clean energy company that develops, builds, owns and operates renewable projects across the island of Ireland, with a portfolio spanning onshore wind, solar and battery energy storage (BESS). From our Cork office, our team supports projects across Munster and the wider island, in one of Europe's most exciting renewable energy markets. We are looking for a graduate analyst to help power that growth.
What you will do
You will work at the analytical heart of the business, supporting decisions across development, finance and operations. Expect variety, real responsibility and plenty of learning. Your work will include:
Building and maintaining models for project economics, energy production and market analysis
Conducting research on markets, policy, technologies and competitors to support strategic decisions
Supporting due diligence on new projects and acquisitions, working with data from every corner of the business
Analysing performance data from our operating fleet and reporting on trends and improvements
Preparing clear reports, dashboards and presentations for project teams and senior leadership
Supporting the development team with data for grid applications, planning and site selection
Improving the spreadsheets, tools and datasets the whole company relies on
What we are looking for
A degree (2.1 or above) in finance, economics, engineering, environmental science, data analytics or a related field
A genuine interest in renewable energy and the clean energy transition
Strong analytical skills and real comfort in Excel; experience with Python, SQL or data visualisation tools is an advantage
Attention to detail and the discipline to get the numbers right
Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to turn analysis into insight
Initiative and curiosity: you take ownership, ask good questions and learn quickly
The right to work in Ireland
Internship or project experience in energy, finance or data analysis is an advantage but not essential. We hire for aptitude and attitude, and we invest in developing our people.
What we offer
€45,000 - €55,000 starting salary, depending on experience
Hybrid working from our Cork office
A structured development path with mentorship from experienced analysts and managers
Exposure to development, finance and operations across three technologies
Pension contributions, generous annual leave and wellbeing support
Support for professional development and further study
The chance to grow with a company building and operating real clean energy assets
How to apply
Apply with your CV and a short note on why this role interests you. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
We are an equal opportunities employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team, and we welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. Reasonable accommodations are available on request at any stage of the recruitment process.

jobs.title: ACG Global Commercialization Manager
jobs.desc:
Job Description
Agilent inspires and supports discoveries that advance the quality of life. We provide life science, diagnostic and applied market laboratories worldwide with instruments, services, consumables, applications and expertise. Agilent enables customers to gain the answers and insights they seek ---- so they can do what they do best: improve the world around us. Information about Agilent is available at www.agilent.com.
We are looking for a Global Commercialization Manager to support our product introduction for the Agilent CrossLab Group (ACG).
The Commercialization Manager will drive consistent commercialization success across our new and existing portfolio within ACG. In this critical role, you will lead and execute the successful launch of our cutting-edge products, ensuring they meet market demands and drive business growth. Your expertise in project management, market analysis, and cross-functional collaboration will be pivotal in delivering innovative solutions to scientists and researchers worldwide.
In this role you will partner directly with key stakeholders across multiple functions including Product Management, Commercial Marketing, Sales Channels, Business Operations, Training & Enablement and Product Support.
Key Responsibilities include:
Develop and implement comprehensive commercialization plans for new life science products, ensuring alignment with Agilent's goals and market needs
Lead and manage multiple launch projects simultaneously, ensuring timely execution, addressing commercialization requirements as per our commercialization playbook.
Lead the commercialization process and governance to drive consistency and efficiency in processes across the ACG organization
Lead division and Field engagements via planning and execution of commercialization milestone meetings to gain commitment on pricing and forecast
Hold multi-functional team accountable to the commercialization planning process to ensure the team meet objectives within the planned launch timeline
Train Product Managers on go to market process and provide consultation on the process
Ensure alignment across Product Management, Commercial Marketing, Field Sales, Training & Enablement to achieve a successful NPI launch and ramp to volume
Partner with Solution unit teams to develop content and insight messaging for new product introductions
Establish key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics to measure launch success, analyze performance data, and make data-driven recommendations for continuous improvement.
The role forms part of the wider Agilent Launch Excellence Team. Launch Excellence consists of Commercialization Managers, Channel Development Managers, as well as a Center of Excellence for optimizing our Commercialization playbook and building appropriate tools to support product launches across the Agilent Enterprise. As a key member of this team, you will partner with the Channel Development Manager to ensure Sales Channel readiness, conduct periodic post launch audits, spearhead commercialization process improvement opportunities, and actively participate on the Launch Excellence CoE.
Personal Attributes:
Proactive and self-motivated with a passion for driving commercial success
Adaptable and able to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
Strong problem-solving skills and a keen attention to detail
Skills:
Strong project management and organizational skills
Excellent communication and presentation abilities
Proven ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team environment
Analytical mindset with the ability to interpret data and make strategic decisions
Knowledge: Familiarity with requirements and standards within the life sciences industry.
Qualifications
Personal Attributes/Skills/Knowledge:
Proactive and self-motivated with a passion for driving commercial success
Adaptable and able to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
Broad scientific industry knowledge. Familiarity with requirements and standards within the industry.
Strong project management and organizational skills
Proven ability to work effectively in a cross-functional team environment with members from different geographies and cultures
Analytical mindset with the ability to interpret data and make strategic decisions
Excellent communication and presentation skills
Job Posting Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master's Degree or equivalent.
Post-graduate, certification, and/or license may be required.
Typically, at least 8+ years relevant experience for entry to this level in one or multiple areas including Product Marketing, Sales Channel, Commercial Marketing, Leading Cross Functional Projects.
Additional Details
This job has a full time weekly schedule. It includes the option to work remotely. Applications for this job will be accepted until at least oktober 14, 2026 or until the job is no longer posted.
The full-time equivalent pay range for this position is $135.840,00 - $212.250,00/yr plus eligibility for bonus, stock and benefits. Our pay ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. At Crowleys DFK we recognise that it’s our people who make us who we are. We pride ourselves on our value-based culture which creates a caring, inclusive, innovative and collaborative environment – a culture where you can take your career to the next level. We celebrate the different skillsets, backgrounds, and talents in all our people and are always looking for experienced professionals to join our team.
If you want to work for a progressive and successful firm, one founded on teamwork and that offers you support at every stage of your career, then that firm is Crowleys DFK!

compensation
package including excellent

.

y

About the opportunity:
Due to exciting and continued growth, our Payroll Services department are looking for an Assistant Manager to join their team. This position will be permanent, full-time, Hybrid(2 days in the office) and based in our Cork office.
Reporting to the Senior Payroll Manager, the Assistant Manager in Payroll Services will support the day-to-day operation of the Payroll Services Department, ensuring the accurate and timely delivery of payroll services to a diverse client portfolio.
This role combines payroll processing, people management, client relationship management and operational oversight. The successful candidate will take ownership of payroll delivery, support and develop team members, drive continuous improvement initiatives and help maintain the high standards of service expected by clients.
The ideal candidate will be technically strong, commercially aware and capable of working independently while providing day-to-day guidance, support and oversight to designated team members. They will be proactive in identifying and resolving issues before they impact clients or the business and will know when matters should be escalated to the Senior Payroll Manager.
Y
ou can expect your duties will primarily include:
Payroll Operations
Process weekly, fortnightly and monthly client payrolls accurately and on time.
Review team payroll outputs and ensure compliance with internal controls and quality standards.
Process timesheets, manual calculations and payroll adjustments.
Handle payroll-related queries with Revenue, pension providers and other third parties.
Calculate statutory payments, holiday and public holiday entitlements.
Ensure compliance with payroll legislation and best practice.
Team & Payroll Management
Supervise, support and develop Payroll Executives.
Manage the delivery of assigned payroll portfolios, ensuring deadlines and service standards are consistently achieved.
Assist with workload planning, resource allocation and payroll scheduling across the team.
Review work completed by team members and provide feedback, coaching and support where required.
Support the training, mentoring and ongoing development of Payroll Executives.
Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Client Management & Business Development
Build and maintain strong client relationships.
Act as an escalation point for payroll queries and issues.
Participate in client meetings and payroll reviews.
Prepare fee quotations and support new business opportunities.
Coordinate the onboarding of new payroll clients.
Technical & Operational Excellence
Develop and maintain expertise in payroll systems, reporting and data import processes.
Create, maintain and troubleshoot payroll reports and imports.
Act as a subject matter expert on payroll processes and systems.
Identify and implement process improvements and efficiencies.
Lead or participate in payroll-related projects and system enhancements.
Maintain process documentation and support knowledge sharing across the team.
Leadership & Risk Management
Take ownership of operational issues and drive them through to resolution.
Monitor the payroll inbox and ensure client queries are dealt with promptly.
Identify risks, issues and service concerns at an early stage.
Escalate matters appropriately and in a timely manner.
Act as deputy to the Senior Payroll Manager, assuming responsibility for the day-to-day management of the department during periods of absence.
Support the achievement of departmental objectives and service standards.
What we are looking for:
Essential
Certified Payroll Technician (IPASS) or Diploma in Payroll Management.
Minimum 5 years' experience processing Irish payrolls, ideally within a payroll bureau, outsourced payroll or multi-client environment.
Strong knowledge of Irish payroll legislation and Revenue requirements.
Strong experience working with payroll software and payroll processing systems; experience using Sage Micropay, MegaPay or equivalent payroll platforms would be a distinct advantage.
Previous experience supervising, mentoring or coordinating the work of other team members.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills.
Excellent organisational, communication and problem-solving skills.
Strong client relationship management skills.
Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
Ability to manage assignments from start to finish with minimal supervision
Excellent client service and stakeholder management skills.
Desirable
Public sector payroll experience.
Experience managing client onboarding and payroll implementations.
Experience creating payroll reports, imports and validation processes.
Experience identifying and implementing process improvements.

jobs.title: Sales Assistant
jobs.desc:
Do you take pride in creating great experiences for others and enjoy working in an environment where no two days are the same. We’re on the lookout for enthusiastic, friendly, and celebration-loving people to join our team as Sales Assistants.
Our stores are places of celebration, creativity, and connection—every day of the year. As things get busier, we’re looking for extra hands and friendly faces to help keep everything running smoothly. If you enjoy being part of a vibrant, welcoming environment, we’d love to have you on the team.
What You’ll Be Getting Up To:
Put our customers at the heart of everything you do — it’s our promise to them.
Make every shopper feel welcomed, wowed, and won over — that’s the cardfactory way!
Serve at the tills with a smile, making sure everyone finds what they came in for (and maybe a little extra).
Keeping our shelves stocked and looking fabulous.
Recommend our amazing range of gifts, wrap, and more — we’re so much more than cards!
No retail experience needed, you’ll be working with a friendly team and receive full training. What matters most is that you’re friendly, approachable, comfortable on your feet (it gets busy, but it’s all part of the fun!) and ready to help. If you’re flexible with your time — we may even offer shifts across nearby stores if you’re up for.
If you’ve got great communication skills, love to chat, whilst gaining valuable experience in a fun and friendly environment, this could be the perfect opportunity for you. At cardfactory, you’ll be part of a supportive team, learning new skills and helping to create memorable moments for every customer who walks through our doors.
Our colleagues tell us — it’s a great team, good vibes, flexible hours and a job they genuinely love. If you’re ready to be a celebration expert, we’d love to hear from you.
There’s no fixed closing date for this role, so we encourage you to apply early as we may close the vacancy once we’ve received enough applications.
No agencies, please.

nd

Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer’s favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move.  Our core purpose is “Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day”.  Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers.  It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. ABEC's unique value is based on combining long experience with the ability to engineer, design, manufacture, commission, qualify, and service the entire bioprocess to reduce overall cost, shorten time to market, and maximise productivity. .

jobs.title: Maintenance Technician
jobs.desc:
The Role
We are seeking an experienced Maintenance Technician to join a busy manufacturing environment. The successful candidate will be responsible for supporting preventative and predictive maintenance programmes, carrying out effective maintenance routines and repairs, and ensuring maximum availability and reliability of site equipment.
You will work closely with Operations, Engineering, Process Engineering, Facilities, contractors and equipment suppliers to minimise downtime and support the efficient running of manufacturing operations.
Key Responsibilities
Provide maintenance support to designated manufacturing areas and ensure maximum equipment uptime.
Carry out preventative, predictive and reactive maintenance on a wide range of manufacturing equipment.
Respond quickly and effectively to equipment breakdowns, minimising production downtime.
Diagnose and repair electrical, electronic, pneumatic and hydraulic faults.
Support the Facilities team and liaise with external contractors when required.
Contribute to reliability-centred maintenance programmes and continuous improvement initiatives.
Support the achievement of strong MTTR (Mean Time to Repair) and MTBF (Mean Time Between Failures) performance.
Promote continuous improvement, innovation and lean manufacturing principles.
Support Total Asset Care and 5S programmes across manufacturing and technical areas.
Assist with new product development and new equipment introduction projects.
Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, including labour hours, spare parts, equipment downtime and repairs, using the site CMMS.
Support the implementation and upkeep of manufacturing equipment excellence programmes.
Ensure all maintenance activities comply with company Health & Safety, Environmental and GMP requirements.
Ensure hazardous and non-hazardous materials are disposed of in accordance with company procedures.
Promote safe and efficient operation of all equipment onsite.
Ensure contractors working within areas of responsibility comply with company safety, environmental and waste management procedures.
Provide timely updates on maintenance activities and work status to relevant maintenance and operations teams.
Adhere to all company procedures and relevant SOPs.
Key Competencies
Strong communication skills.
Highly motivated with a strong work ethic.
Excellent problem-solving and diagnostic ability.
Flexible and adaptable approach to work.
Ability to use initiative and demonstrate innovation.
Strong team player.
Professional, tactful and diplomatic approach.
Continuous improvement mindset.
Essential Qualifications & Experience
Strong electrical and electronic repair and diagnostic skills.
Experience in pneumatic and hydraulic fault finding and repair.
Good understanding of robotics and automated manufacturing systems.
Experience working with high-speed manufacturing equipment.
Experience maintaining and troubleshooting vision systems.
Knowledge of Windows networking.
Some programming experience.
Knowledge of PLCs, drives and HMIs.
Ability to apply strong theoretical knowledge to practical maintenance situations.
Experience working within an FDA-regulated manufacturing environment and understanding of GMP requirements.
Previous experience working in a cleanroom environment.
Strong computer skills.
Third-level qualification in Automation, Mechatronics or a related discipline.
Willingness and ability to travel for a minimum of 3 months for training.
Desirable Experience
Previous experience using a CMMS, preferably Maximo, within a maintenance environment.
3–5 years' experience in an FDA-regulated manufacturing/maintenance environment.
Experience with label printers and label placement equipment.
Experience with FactoryTalk ProductionCentre, Rockwell or SCADA systems.
For more information please call Christina Keating on 0
21 494 4871 or email christina.keating@cpl.ie

jobs.desc:
Company Overview
At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future.
Department Overview
At Motorola Solutions, we're guided by a shared purpose—helping people be their best in the moments that matter. We live up to our purpose every day by solving for safer, building mission-critical communications devices and networks, AI-powered video security, and integrated command center views. The work we do connects public safety agencies and enterprises to enable vital collaboration when it matters the most.
Our RFSite Software Engineering organization, a key component of the Critical Communications Networks business segment, consists of a diverse group of software engineers, product architects, system architects, and test engineers across global locations.
We leverage the latest virtualization technologies on a robust Linux platform, following modern software development practices such as Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD), DevOps, and automated testing. Operating within Agile/Scrum methodologies, our team is responsible for the end-to-end software development lifecycle of next-generation Radio Frequency (RF) Site solutions.
Job Description
We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to join an Agile Scrum team developing containerized Linux user-space applications and services for mission-critical land mobile radio communications products.
In this role, you will focus on writing high-quality modern Python services deployed in container environments and leveraging AI tools/technologies to accelerate development, while interfacing with and debugging existing C++ subsystems. You will apply solid Linux OS and networking fundamentals, leverage multiple automated testing frameworks, and work in an RF telecommunications context alongside modern CI/CD tooling.
Key Responsibilities
Containerized Service Development: Design, implement, and maintain Linux user-space applications using modern Python constructs within containerized environments.
AI Tooling & Integration: Utilize approved AI-assisted development tools and integrate AI/ML capabilities or automated analytics into engineering workflows where applicable.
Linux OS & Networking: Develop networking applications utilizing socket programming, network protocol handling (TCP/IP, UDP), and Linux OS user-space interactions.
Automated Testing Ecosystem: Build and expand test suites for unit, integration, and end-to-end testing.
System Interfacing & Debugging: Read, interface with, and debug lower-level legacy or embedded C/C++ codebases and APIs.
RF & Telecommunications Context: Work with RF domain concepts, radio infrastructure, and network protocols during product integration.
CI/CD & Quality Assurance: Integrate code into automated build pipelines and enforce code quality standards using static analysis.
On-Site Lab Testing: Engage in hands-on testing, configuration, and debugging across virtualized environments and physical RF site equipment/network gear.
Basic Requirements
Education & Experience
Bachelor’s (BS) degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field with relevant software engineering experience, OR
Master’s (MS) degree with relevant work experience.
Primary Language: Demonstrated proficiency in software development using modern Python.
Linux OS & Networking: Strong understanding of Linux operating system concepts, user-space architecture, and networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, sockets, network protocols).
Containers: Practical experience with Linux user-space development and containerization platforms.
Automated Testing: Hands-on experience automated testing frameworks.
C/C++ Knowledge: Ability to read, interface with, and debug C/C++ codebases.
Desired Skills & Experience
Exposure to AI/ML tools (e.g., AI coding assistants, prompt engineering for developer tooling, or integration of AI APIs/frameworks).
Familiarity or background in RF / Telecommunications / Land Mobile Radio (LMR) systems.
Experience with CI/CD tools and static code analysis tools.
Version control and task management using Git and Jira.
Experience with network diagnostic tools.
Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills in a cross-functional team.

THE OPPORTUNITY
We have an exciting opportunity for a skilled and motivated Hydrologist to join our growing water and environment team at Stantec. You will play a key role in delivering hydrological assessments and technical inputs across a wide range of infrastructure, water, and development projects, with excellent opportunities to develop your career within a multidisciplinary environment.
About The Role
This is a strong opportunity to join a growing and well-established water and environment team at a time of continued expansion, where you can make a meaningful impact on a diverse portfolio of infrastructure, water, and development projects. As part of a multidisciplinary organisation, you will gain exposure to a broad range of technical challenges while collaborating with experts across engineering, environmental, and planning disciplines.
You will have the chance to take ownership of key hydrological assessments, contribute to high-profile projects, and develop your expertise in flood risk management, drainage, and environmental reporting within the Irish regulatory framework. The role offers a clear pathway for career progression, supported by ongoing professional development, mentoring, and opportunities to expand your technical and project management skills.
Being part of a larger international organisation provides access to global best practices, innovative tools, and a wide professional network, while still maintaining a strong local presence and project focus. This is an ideal role for someone looking to advance their career in hydrology, deepen their technical capabilities, and contribute to sustainable water management and climate resilience solutions.
YOUR IMPACT
In this role, you will play a key part in shaping how water is managed across a variety of projects, helping to ensure that development is both sustainable and resilient to future climate challenges. Your work will directly inform critical decisions around flood risk, drainage design, and environmental protection, influencing outcomes for communities, infrastructure, and natural ecosystems.
By delivering robust hydrological assessments and clear, evidence-based insights, you will support clients and project teams in navigating complex regulatory requirements and achieving successful project approvals. Your input will contribute to reducing flood risk, improving water quality, and promoting sustainable development practices across Ireland.
You will also strengthen collaboration within multidisciplinary teams, bringing a hydrology perspective that enhances overall project quality and innovation. Through your technical expertise and proactive approach, you will help drive high standards, build client confidence, and contribute to the continued growth and reputation of the team.
About You
You are a motivated hydrology professional with experience in surface water assessments, data analysis, and environmental reporting within the Irish regulatory context. You have a solid understanding of flood risk management, drainage design principles, and relevant legislation and guidance. With strong analytical, communication, and report-writing skills, you work effectively both independently and as part of multidisciplinary teams. You are enthusiastic about sustainable water management and committed to delivering high-quality technical outputs that support positive environmental outcomes.
Your Technical Skills Include
Undertaking hydrological assessments including flood risk assessments (FRA), drainage impact assessments, and surface water studies.
Collecting, analysing, and interpreting hydrological and meteorological data.
Supporting the preparation of technical reports and environmental submissions, including EIAR inputs and regulatory assessments.
Contributing to project scoping, planning, and programming activities.
You are adaptable and capable of managing challenging workloads under changing priorities, delivering high-quality results in a dynamic environment.

We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025. =
We do what is right: Industry leading training and development as well as paid for professional subscriptions. A professional progression plan, supporting you to become chartered.
We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment to assist with the growth of your career.
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the Ireland - we want you to be part of it!

Join our Motor Division as a Claims Handler, managing a portfolio of motor damage claims for key clients.

Technical Claims Knowledge – The ideal candidate will have knowledge of how to assess both liability and quantum, the investigations to be undertaken and a good understanding of motor coverages generally. .
Investigation & Decision Making – Confident carrying out desktop liability investigations, reviewing evidence, determining liability and making accurate, well-reasoned decisions.
Customer, Client & Complaint Handling – Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with a customer-focused approach, confidence liaising with clients and colleagues, and complaint handling experience considered advantageous.
Negotiation & Claims Resolution – Strong negotiating, influencing and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate and settle claims in a timely, compliant and commercially aware manner.
Attention to Detail & Accuracy – High levels of accuracy and attention to detail when reviewing documentation, assessing claims and maintaining records.
Adaptability & Resilience – Able to thrive in a dynamic and target-driven environment, managing deadlines, changing priorities and business needs with a positive and flexible approach.

1890 41 61 41. Press Option 4 and quote your driver number.

Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren’t limited to:
A variety of shifts
Part time and full time contracts available between 20 -  39 hours   a week
An hourly rate of pay for new drivers of €18.24 per hour with additional premium for Sunday working

Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2
nd
Clubcard available.*

Pension Plan*

Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme

Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer’s favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move.  Our core purpose is “Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day”.  Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers.  It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children’s Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
