jobs.title: Engineering Quality & Excellence Manager
jobs.desc:
Who We Are
Build what matters. Grow where it counts.
At AMCS, sustainability means business — and careers that create impact. From our roots in Ireland to our teams across Europe, North America and Australasia, we are bringing together ambitious people to help reshape the industries that sustain our world.
What We Build
We build intelligent, cloud-based SaaS solutions that turn complex operations into smarter, more sustainable performance. Powered by AI, data and deep industry expertise, our technology helps customers optimise routes, manage recycling, improve compliance, unlock insight and move faster toward a more efficient, circular future.
Why Join AMCS
Join AMCS and be part of a global team where purpose meets performance. Here, you can grow your career, challenge what’s possible and work on technology that makes a measurable difference — for our customers, our communities and the planet.
Due to the continued level of growth at AMCS, we have an opportunity for a highly motivated and experienced Engineering Quality & Excellence Manager.
This role exists to scale engineering standards and quality practices across the entire global Engineering organisation. It defines what good engineering looks like at AMCS, measures whether the organisation is actually doing it, and drives Engineering Managers to close the gaps.
This role becomes the operational owner of the engineering excellence system: senior Engineering leadership sets strategy and expectations; this role turns those expectations into standards, measurement, governance and improvement programmes; Engineering Managers remain accountable for implementing them in their teams.
What You'll Do
Define, own and evolve the global engineering standards that describe what good engineering looks like across all products and teams — covering source control, code review, CI/CD, testing, static analysis, security and observability.
Own the global engineering maturity model and the scorecard derived from it, running assessments that give senior Engineering leadership a credible view of quality, risk and trend.
Use data to identify systemic quality and engineering risk, and drive improvement programmes with Engineering Managers, holding them accountable for closing gaps in their own teams.
Provide strategic leadership to the Quality Engineering function through the Quality Engineering Manager, targeting quality engineering investment at the highest-risk areas.
Act as the central Engineering point of contact for engineering-related compliance and audit requirements, translating them into concrete engineering expectations and coordinating Engineering's response.
Partner with Engineering Managers on capability building while holding the line on standards — leading primarily through influence and credible data rather than line authority.
Own reporting to senior Engineering leadership — providing the metrics, updates and status on engineering quality and maturity.
What You'll Bring
Substantial experience in senior engineering, engineering quality or engineering excellence leadership roles within a multi-product software organisation.
Deep understanding of modern engineering practice — source control strategy, code review, CI/CD, test automation strategy, static analysis, performance engineering, observability and secure development — with enough depth to credibly challenge Engineering Managers on any of them.
Strong command of engineering and quality metrics, and the judgement to distinguish a meaningful signal from a metric that will be gamed.
Proven ability to drive change across organisational boundaries through influence, evidence and governance rather than line authority.
Experience defining and running a maturity model, assessment framework or engineering standards programme at scale.
Experience of regulatory or audit frameworks such as SOC 2, PCI DSS or ISO 27001 from the engineering side, including evidence and remediation.
Comfortable operating globally across time zones, cultures and engineering teams with different histories and maturity levels.
Credible with engineers without needing to be a hands-on developer — genuine technical literacy and the confidence to hold a technical argument.
Resilient and direct, able to deliver unwelcome findings to peers and hold the standard under delivery pressure.
How Success Will Be Measured (first 12 Months)
Demonstrable improvement in engineering maturity scores across the portfolio, with the weakest teams improving fastest.
Reduction in customer-found and escaped defects, and improvement in release quality.
Increased consistency of engineering practice across products, measured against the standards rather than asserted.
Engineering quality risk identified proactively from data rather than surfacing through customer impact or escalation.
Engineering compliance obligations met on time, with evidence available and audits passing without engineering-side surprises.
Quality Engineering investment demonstrably targeted at the highest-risk areas.
Engineering Managers treating the scorecard as a useful management tool rather than an imposed reporting exercise.

jobs.title: Senior Proposal Specialist

Working closely with Business Development Managers, clinical subject matter experts and operational teams, you will help develop accurate, customised and commercially competitive responses to RFPs and RFIs.

Develop and coordinate complex proposal responses and Statements of Work (SOWs) in line with RFP requirements and Sponsor expectations

Develop initial clinical trial costing assumptions and populate CRO costings, working with clinical experts to refine and finalise budgets
Obtain and incorporate pre-award budgets from vendors and site partners and ensure overall costing is accurate and ready for executive review
Coordinate internal contributors, manage actions and timelines, and ensure all required proposal content is delivered on schedule
Support BD Managers with RFIs, client meetings, budget discussions, presentations and, where required, bid defence activities
Clearly communicate and explain final costing assumptions to internal and external stakeholders and support amendments, updates and change orders
Conduct market research and literature reviews when required to strengthen the accuracy and quality of proposal responses
Contribute to BD tools, reporting and process improvements, and support project hand-off activities for awarded studies and Sponsors
Skills & Qualifications
Post-secondary certificate/diploma required; a Bachelor’s degree, preferably in Science or a related discipline, is an advantage
4–6 years of relevant experience preferred, with an equivalent combination of education and experience considered
Previous budget development/costing experience within a CRO and/or clinical trials environment is mandatory
Strong understanding of clinical trial processes and the ability to interpret study requirements and translate them into accurate proposals and budgets
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and strong working knowledge of other Microsoft Office applications
Strong project coordination and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines and stakeholders
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to work with both internal teams and external Sponsors
Highly detail-oriented, analytical and logical, with a structured and process-driven approach to problem solving
Ability to work independently while effectively collaborating with cross-functional teams and subject matter experts
Fluent in English, both written and verbal
What We Offer
In addition, as an Alimentiv Employee, you’re also eligible for the following programs:
Education Reimbursement program for full-time employees
Monthly Cell Phone and Remote Work Allowance (dependent on role eligibility)
One time office setup allowance (can be used to purchase a scanner/printer, extra monitor, office furniture, etc.)
Working while visiting program – up to 4 weeks per year!
Flexible Summer Hours Program from May – September
Employee referral incentive – we know great people know other great people, and we think that warrants recognition!
Full-time employees also become beneficiaries of the Alimentiv Trust after one year of employment, and permanent members after 5 years of employment
Optional formal mentorship program (Alimentorship); country/region annual social events in person; leadership development programs for people leaders in accordance with your seniority; social committee and several other optional initiatives designed to support you in feeling like part of the Alimentiv team!
Additional benefits may be available depending on the country of employment and are subject to local policies and eligibility.
Our Services
End-to-end GI clinical trial services, from protocol design through submission support
Central medical imaging management and endoscopic reading
Precision medicine and biomarker solutions
Real-world evidence and clinical consulting
Histopathology and lab services through AcelaBio
How to Apply
To apply for this position, please submit your resume through the Alimentiv Careers Portal or via LinkedIn’s Easy Apply. Resumes must be submitted in English.
Equal Opportunity and Accessibility
Alimentiv is committed to building a diverse, inclusive and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, ethnicity, national origin, religion or belief, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital or family status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
Accommodations are available upon request for persons with disabilities throughout the recruitment and selection process. Requests can be directed to recruitment@alimentiv.com.
Stay Alert to Recruitment Scams
Alimentiv is aware of a continued increase in phishing scams, which use various methods of attack via email, text, voice and social media, including individuals posing as our recruiters and contacting candidates with fraudulent opportunities. Our hiring process always includes direct engagement with a recruiter or hiring manager, and we will never ask for sensitive personal information early in the process.
Official communication will only come from company email addresses containing "@alimentiv.com". If you are contacted about an open job at Alimentiv, please verify the domain of the sender's email address and confirm that you are being asked to apply on this website. If something doesn't feel right, we encourage you to verify before responding. If you believe you have been the victim of a phishing scam, please contact your local government cyber authority to report it.
We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

jobs.title: Post-Doc for BioShore project on biostimulants from seaweeds
jobs.desc:
Company Description
South East Technological University (SETU) is a dynamic higher education institution whose mission is to engage, learn, challenge, and innovate. In a vibrant environment for creative teaching and research, WIT fosters lifelong learning, exploration, and discovery with a strong global outlook. The institute blends theoretical and applied inquiry, integrating scholarly, professional, and vocational pursuits with scientific and creative expression. WIT is committed to access, equality of opportunity, and progression, empowering learners to succeed in a complex world. Through collaboration with regional communities, education partners, and public and private agencies, WIT advances excellence in globally benchmarked higher education and knowledge.
Role Description
This full-time, on-site Post-Doctoral Researcher role is based in County Waterford, Ireland and focuses on the BioShore project investigating biostimulants derived from seaweeds. The post-doc will design and execute laboratory experiments related to seaweed-based biostimulants, including extraction, characterization, and evaluation of their effects on plant growth and resilience. Day-to-day activities will involve managing experimental protocols, collecting and analyzing research data, preparing technical reports, and contributing to peer-reviewed publications and conference presentations. The role includes collaborative work with multidisciplinary teams, participation in project meetings, and engagement with industry and academic partners as needed. The post-doc may also contribute to mentoring students and supporting teaching activities aligned with the project’s research goals.
Qualifications
Candidates should possess strong Laboratory Skills, including experimental design, sample preparation, and safe handling of biological and chemical materials.
Candidates should possess Research and Data Analysis skills, including literature review, statistical analysis, and interpretation of complex datasets.
Candidates should possess relevant Physics knowledge where applicable to material characterization, fluid dynamics, or other physical processes involved in biostimulant development.
Candidates should possess Teaching and mentoring abilities to support student supervision, training in laboratory methods, and occasional contributions to instructional activities.
PhD in a relevant discipline (e.g., Biotechnology, Plant Science, Marine Science, Chemistry, Environmental Science, or related field).
Experience with seaweed or other marine biomass, biostimulants, plant physiology, or agricultural applications is highly desirable.
Proficiency in scientific writing, including preparation of manuscripts, reports, and grant proposals.
Ability to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams, manage project timelines, and communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

jobs.desc:

See it differently
You see the world through a unique lens and that’s exactly what we need. We embrace how you see things differently – it’s essential for creating a sustainable future.
Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates and students who help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities.
The Opportunity
We are currently seeking a Work Placement geoenvironmental scientist/engineer to join our specialist Ground Engineering team in Cork or Dublin, Ireland. The team provides geological, geoenvironmental, hydrogeological and geotechnical input to a portfolio of exciting, varied and multidisciplinary projects across Ireland and internationally. Our work spans major infrastructure, energy, water, environmental and development projects, with a strong focus on understanding land and groundwater quality conditions and managing environmental risks
During your work placement at Arup, you will work alongside a team on tasks such as:
Geological, geoenvironmental, hydrogeological and geotechnical desk studies, site assessments and development of conceptual site models.
Planning and interpretation of ground investigations, including drilling, trial pitting, rock coring, geological logging, and soil and water sampling.
Assessment and interpretation of geochemical data to determine impacts on land and water quality.
Review options for the sustainable use of soils and stone during construction projects
Groundwater contaminant transport modelling to assess to need for remediation or assessing the potential impacts of the re-use of materials.
Preparation of technical reports, geoenvironmental assessments, and environmental documentation.
Geoenvironmental input to Environmental Impact Assessment Reports (EIARs), and regulatory submissions.
Working closely with specialists from other disciplines to develop integrated and sustainable engineering solutions.
Attending project meetings and communicating with colleagues, project partners, contractors, regulators and clients.

Changemakers: A passion for sustainable development and creating a better world is key.

We are a financially strong international company with a culture that maintains the fast-paced, creative environment of a startup. The Role:
The Credit and Collections Manager, EMEA is responsible for leading Credit, Collections and Cash Application activities across the EMEA region while maintaining ownership of a designated customer portfolio. The role combines people leadership, credit risk management, collections strategy, operational oversight, escalation management, process improvement and cross-functional stakeholder management.
The position is accountable for driving cash collection performance, minimizing credit risk exposure, overseeing cash application and Accounts Receivable activities, coordinating month-end closing requirements and ensuring the consistent execution of global Order-to-Cash processes. The Manager serves as the primary escalation point for complex customer, credit and collections matters and provides functional leadership for continuous improvement initiatives, system implementations and global business transformation projects.
Essential Functions:
Team Leadership and Operational Management
Lead, coach, develop and motivate a team of Credit, Collections and Cash Application professionals through performance management, objective setting, succession planning, career development, capacity planning and workload prioritization.
Build a high-performing team culture focused on accountability, collaboration, continuous learning and operational excellence.
Portfolio and Collections Management
Manage a customer portfolio, driving collection performance, overdue debt reduction and DSO improvements across the EMEA region.
Collaborate with customers and internal stakeholders to resolve issues impacting collection activities and accelerate payment resolution.
Cash Application Oversight
Monitor unapplied, unidentified and incorrectly allocated cash balances and work with relevant internal teams and customers to obtain remittance information and resolve allocation issues.
Credit Risk Management
Lead customer credit assessments, financial analysis, credit limit approvals and risk mitigation activities across the EMEA portfolio.
Monitor customer exposure, payment behavior and portfolio risk, implementing actions to minimize financial risk and bad debt.
Exercise delegated credit authority and ensure credit decisions are appropriately documented and compliant with company policies and controls.
Partner with Sales and Order Management to achieve timely resolution of orders placed on credit hold while balancing risk management and commercial objectives.
Escalation and Stakeholder Management
Build effective relationships with internal stakeholders and act as the primary regional escalation point for complex customer issues, credit challenges, collection disputes and order release decisions.
Communicate significant portfolio risks, overdue balances and recommended actions to senior management and key stakeholders, while coordinating actions, owners and timelines across relevant functions.
Month-End Closing and Financial Controls
Review aging, unapplied cash, customer credit balances, bad debt exposure and other relevant Accounts Receivable balances as part of the month-end close.
Coordinate monthly Accounts Receivable closing activities, ensuring reconciliations are completed, documented, reviewed and submitted in line with SOX requirements, internal controls, company policies and applicable regulatory requirements.
Identify control gaps and implement sustainable corrective actions.
Support internal and external audits by providing documentation, financial analysis and timely responses to audit requests. Coordinate and monitor any remediation actions arising from audits or control reviews.
Reporting and Performance Oversight
Monitor Credit, Collections and Cash Application performance through regular operational reviews, using data and insights to drive prioritization, decision-making and performance improvement.
Analyze key operational and risk metrics to identify trends, root causes and actions required to improve cash flow, reduce risk and optimize performance.
Provide timely and insightful reporting on portfolio performance, risks and recommended actions to management and key stakeholders.
Continuous Improvement, Automation and AI
Foster a culture of continuous improvement and champion the adoption of automation, AI and data-driven tools by encouraging the team to challenge existing processes, identify inefficiencies, eliminate non-value-added activities, strengthen controls and reduce manual effort to improve operational performance and customer experience.
Track the benefits of improvement initiatives and ensure that agreed changes are embedded into standard ways of working.
Projects and Functional Leadership
Lead and participate in global Order-to-Cash transformation initiatives involving SAP, BlackLine and other systems, AI-enabled solutions, e-invoicing, global process standardization, compliance requirements and other capabilities.
Provide leadership and subject matter expertise during business process design, solution development, testing, implementation, cutover and stabilization phases of transformation initiatives and system enhancements, including process documentation, training, communications and stakeholder engagement.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
Strong understanding of Order-to-Cash (OTC) processes and knowledge of Credit, Collections, Cash Application and credit risk management principles.
Proven ability to drive cash collection performance, reduce risk exposure and improve Days Sales Outstanding through effective portfolio management, data analysis and prioritization.
Demonstrated leadership experience, including coaching, performance management, talent development, resource planning and workload prioritization.
Strong analytical and decision-making skills, with the ability to assess risk, identify trends, resolve escalations and balance commercial objectives with sound credit practices.
Excellent organizational, stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate across all levels of the organization.
Knowledge of SOX requirements, internal controls, audit processes and financial compliance standards.
Continuous improvement mindset and curiosity for emerging technologies with a proven ability to streamline processes, leverage automation and eliminate non-value-added activities.
Experience leading or participating in process improvement, system implementation and business transformation initiatives, including process design, testing, implementation and stabilization.
Advanced Microsoft skills. SAP or other ERP experience preferred.
Minimum Education and Work Experience:
We're looking for talented people who are excited about making an impact. Even if your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification listed, we encourage you to apply.
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related discipline preferred but not essential.
7+ years of progressive experience in Accounts Receivable, Credit & Collections, or Finance preferred, including experience managing an individual customer portfolio.
Minimum 2 years of people-management experience.
Demonstrated experience managing customer credit risk and collection activities and coordinating month-end closing activities within a multinational organization, Shared Services, Global Business Services (GBS) or Finance Operation

What is the opportunity?
Key Responsibilities
As a Direct Tax Manager, you will own the direct tax accounting and related compliance for Omnissa’s international group, covering 20+ legal entities. You will also assist in standing up new global processes, including Pillar Two and CbC Reporting. This is great opportunity to get involved in influencing compliance processes at an early stage. The role involves collaborating with other Finance teams, external consultants and continuously working on process improvements for statutory and tax compliance. Here is a breakdown of what you can expect:
Prepare and review quarterly and annual direct tax accruals, current and deferred tax provisions, and effective tax rate analysis for 20+ entities, predominantly international subsidiaries.
Own the tax provision-to-return reconciliation and maintain supporting documentation for deferred tax balances, uncertain tax positions and valuation allowances.
Assist on implementation for Pillar Two processes, including safe harbour testing, GloBE data collection, top-up tax modelling and readiness for GIR / local filing obligations.
Support Country-by-Country Reporting and related notifications, ensuring consistency with statutory accounts, transfer pricing documentation and group reporting data.
Manage the US R&D tax credit process end to end coordinating technical and financial input, and working with advisors to prepare and defend claims.
Manage the direct tax compliance calendar across all international jurisdictions, ensuring returns, payments and elections are filed accurately and on time.
Coordinate with external advisors and outsourced providers on the preparation and review of corporate income tax returns.
Support transfer pricing operations, including intercompany reconciliations and settlements, cost-plus reviews, and maintenance of intercompany agreements and local file documentation.
Reconcile direct tax accounts and support month & quarter end close accruals and ARCS reconciliations.
Manage notices, queries and audits from international and US tax authorities, and act as a primary point of contact for revenue authorities and advisors.
Monitor legislative developments across the group footprint and assess the impact on the group’s tax position, accruals and processes.
Partner with finance, legal, treasury and the wider global accounting team, and contribute to process design, automation and control improvements as the function scales.
Support special projects, including entity rationalisation, restructuring and cross-border transactions, as assigned.
What will you bring to Omnissa?
ACA/ACCA/CPA/CIMA and/or AITI (or equivalent) qualified.
Post qualification experience in direct/corporate tax, gained in practice, industry, or a combination of both.
Strong technical grounding in corporate tax accounting and the ability to prepare and review tax provisions under US GAAP and/or IFRS.
Practical exposure to multinational group compliance and international tax concepts; familiarity with Pillar Two and Country-by-Country Reporting is a distinct advantage.
Working knowledge of transfer pricing principles and intercompany transaction flows is desirable.
Experience with R&D tax credit claims would be an advantage but not essential.
Comfortable building processes where none currently exist, and able to move from technical analysis to practical implementation.
Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel; experience with ERP and tax provision or reporting tools.
Must be meticulous, detail oriented, organised and self-motivated.
Ability to work independently and with cross-functional teams, including non-tax stakeholders.
Ability to be flexible while working with time constraints and deadlines.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to explain technical positions clearly to a non-specialist audience.

jobs.desc:
About the role
At Tesco, we see the value in you –and right now we are hiring Customer Delivery Drivers to join our team
Our core purpose is to serve Irish shoppers a little better every day and being a
Customer Delivery Driver
you are the first face our customers see.
Being a Customer Delivery Driver is hands on, physical and full of variety. No two shifts are ever the same – customer’s look for help in all kinds of different ways.

Various shifts available

Serving your customer with a smile and greet them by name

You will need
To have had a full IRISH or EU driving licence (manual or automatic) for at least 2 years with no more than 3 penalty points
To be a safe and courteous drivers
To enjoy helping others
To be personable with a good sense of humour and excellent communication skills
The ability to take the initiative and use common sense
To care about making a difference for customers and colleagues
The ability to stay calm under pressure
Please be aware that as part of our recruitment process, job offers are subject to the Garda Vetting Process and you will need to provide proof of current penalty points on your licence at Assessment Stage. This can be requested from the National Driver Licence Services (NDLS) on
1890 41 61 41. Press Option 4 and quote your driver number.
We are sorry but if you have been disqualified from driving within the last 10 years, we will not be able to accept your application.
Should you be successful in your application, your offer will be subject to and conditional upon you providing your bank account details before your agreed start date.
Whats in it for you?
We offer excellent benefits that help make Tesco a great place to work. These include but aren’t limited to:
A variety of shifts
Part time and full time contracts available between 20 -  39 hours   a week
An hourly rate of pay for new drivers of €18.24 per hour with additional premium for Sunday working
Annual Bonus Scheme
Colleague Clubcard offering 10% discount across stores and online, with 15% discount weekends once a month (Friday to Sunday), and 20% off twice a year. There is also 20% off F&F clothing, all year long, these various discounts can be extended to a family member with a 2
nd
Clubcard available.*
Our Virtual GP service provides free and confidential access to an online GP through video GP consultations, and online prescription service for colleagues. The service is also available to families of colleagues who live at the same address for a reduced cost.
24/7 access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) for you and family members for in the moment emotional support along with free access to a range of wellbeing services supporting you under our new Wellbeing First approach of Body, Mind and Life.
Life Assurance
Pension Plan*
Save As You Earn Scheme*
Paid Family Leave
Bike to Work
Long Service Awards
Commuter Scheme
*Entry requirements and rules of the scheme apply
About Us
Our vision at Tesco is to become every customer’s favourite way to shop, whether they are at home or out on the move.  Our core purpose is “Serving our customers, communities and planet a little better every day”.  Serving means more than a transactional relationship with our customers.  It means acting as a responsible and sustainable business for all stakeholders, for the communities we are part of, and for the planet. Through initiatives like the Tesco Community Fund, our association with Children’s Health Foundation, our partnership with FoodCloud and our Stronger Starts programme, we have supported over 21,000 community groups, raised over €7.5 million for medical equipment, and provided almost 15 million meals nationwide, to those living in food insecurity.
Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated.   At Tesco, we not only celebrate diversity, but recognise the value and opportunity it brings.  We always want our colleagues to feel they can be themselves at work and we are committed to helping them be at their best.
We know life looks a little different for each of us. That’s why at Tesco, we always welcome chats about flexible working. Some people are at the start of their careers, some want the freedom to do the things they love. Others are going through life-changing moments like becoming a carer, nearing retirement, adapting to parenthood, or something else. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.
Tesco is committed to celebrating diversity and everyone is welcome at Tesco. We're committed to providing a fully inclusive recruitment process, allowing candidates the opportunity to thrive and inform us of any reasonable adjustments they may require. For further information on the accessibility support we can offer, please click http://roi.tesco-careers.com/accessibility/

tescoireland.recruitment@tesco.ie
This will allow us to understand more about you and how we can best support you through the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Business Analyst (Automation & AI)
jobs.desc:
Department
: AI & Automation, Musgrave Group
Reports to
: AI Programme Manager
Location:
Cork office, operating under Musgrave's Work Smart hybrid working model
Travel
: Regular travel to Musgrave and project sites across Ireland is required for workshops, meetings, training and project activities
Join Musgrave: Where Innovation Meets Heritage, and People Drive Change
Musgrave is one of Europe’s most successful family-owned businesses, with a rich 150-year legacy in food and brand innovation. We`re proud to serve communities across Ireland and Spain, feeding one in three people every day through iconic brands like SuperValu, Centra, Mace, Frank and Honest, and Musgrave MarketPlace. By supporting thousands of retail and foodservice family businesses, we make a positive impact on the communities they serve. We`re committed to becoming the most trusted and sustainable business in Ireland, and we`re looking for dynamic, forward-thinking individuals to join us on this journey.
As we continue our journey toward becoming Ireland’s most trusted and sustainable business, we have an exciting opportunity for a successful candidate to join our team as a Business Analyst (Automation & AI).
This is a hands-on, stakeholder-facing Business Analyst role within Musgrave’s AI & Automation function. The role will focus primarily on automation initiatives, with opportunities to support selected AI use cases as the portfolio develops. The successful candidate will combine robust business analysis practices with practical technical knowledge of automation tools and technologies.
You will work within cross-functional delivery teams to identify and assess opportunities, lead in-person discovery and requirements sessions, document processes and requirements to a high standard, and support delivery from initial analysis through implementation, adoption and benefits tracking. You will also deliver business-facing Automation and AI training sessions and contribute confidently to innovation activities, including hackathons.
Please note that this is a 12 month contract
What You’ll Be Doing
Requirements Elicitation and Business Analysis
Lead structured requirements elicitation through in-person workshops, stakeholder interviews, process walkthroughs, observation and document analysis.
Engage confidently with non-technical colleagues, ask effective questions and draw out underlying business, process, data and technical needs.
Document functional and non-functional requirements clearly and unambiguously using agreed Musgrave templates and standards.
Produce and maintain Business Requirements Documents (BRDs), Process Definition Documents (PDDs), Requirements Traceability Matrices (RTMs), user stories, acceptance criteria and related analysis artefacts.
Define scope, assumptions, dependencies, constraints, business rules, exception paths and measurable success criteria.
Maintain clear traceability from business need and requirement through design, delivery, testing and business acceptance
Process Discovery, Modelling and Automation Assessment
Lead process discovery sessions with business stakeholders to understand current ways of working and identify suitable automation opportunities.
Develop and maintain clear As-Is and To-Be process models using Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN) and agreed process-modelling standards.
Assess process suitability, complexity, volumes, variations, exceptions, controls, data requirements, system interactions and operational risks.
Identify practical process improvements and opportunities to simplify or standardise processes before automation.
Work with technical colleagues to evaluate potential approaches using robotic process automation, workflow automation, intelligent document processing and related technologies.
Stakeholder Facilitation, Presentation and Training
Plan and lead engaging in-person workshops, discovery sessions, working groups and playback sessions with operational, business and technical stakeholders.
Present findings, process models, requirements, options and recommendations clearly to audiences with differing levels of technical knowledge.
Facilitate constructive discussion, challenge assumptions respectfully, resolve ambiguity and build agreement on scope, requirements and next steps.
Deliver in-person Automation and AI awareness, training and knowledge-sharing sessions for business colleagues.
Create clear, practical and accessible presentation and training materials that translate technical concepts into business language.
Facilitate solution demonstrations, feedback sessions and business-readiness activities throughout delivery.
Agile Delivery and Requirements Management
Translate business needs and requirements into a structured hierarchy of epics, features and user stories, with clear acceptance criteria and an appropriate level of detail for delivery.
Decompose larger requirements into manageable backlog items while preserving alignment to the agreed business objective, scope and expected value.
Create, refine and maintain backlog items using Azure DevOps, Jira or similar Agile delivery tools.
Work with business stakeholders, the Project Manager, developers, architects, process owners and testers to clarify priorities, assumptions, dependencies and sequencing.
Support backlog refinement and sprint planning by ensuring proposed items are sufficiently analysed, understood and ready for delivery.
Maintain end-to-end traceability from business need through requirements, epics, features, user stories, acceptance criteria, testing, business acceptance and delivered outcomes.
Work with the relevant business owner and delivery team to validate priorities and acceptance decisions; the role supports informed prioritisation but does not own product strategy or technical design.
Support test planning, User Acceptance Testing, defect clarification and confirmation that delivered solutions meet agreed business requirements.
Participate actively in sprint planning, backlog refinement, demonstrations, retrospectives and other Agile delivery ceremonies.
Act as the primary contact for requirements clarification throughout design, build, testing and implementation, supporting timely decisions where ambiguity arises.
Technical Collaboration and Innovation
Apply practical knowledge of automation platforms and technologies when shaping requirements and assessing delivery options.
Collaborate effectively with developers and solution architects, contributing constructively to design discussions without replacing technical design ownership.

RIGHT. Group is a leading engineering solutions provider headquartered in Castleisland, Co. Kerry. We deliver innovative and sustainable engineering services specialising in Water and Wastewater. Our reputation for excellence and commitment to quality has driven significant growth, and we are now seeking a Project Engineer with Electrical experience to join our dynamic team.
Role Overview
The Project Engineer (Electrical) will contribute to the design and delivery of electrical and control systems across water and wastewater projects. The role combines electrical design, control system definition and project coordination, client specifications and Uisce Éireann standards. While proficiency in electrical CAD and schematic development is desirable, the position offers exposure to a wide range of engineering activities including LV distribution and panel design, motor control, SCADA and PLC integration, and site commissioning.

■ Develop and interpret single line diagrams, schematics, panel general arrangements, cable schedules and termination schedules.

THE OPPORTUNITY
At Stantec Ireland, you’ll join a growing Energy team at the forefront of a transforming transmission and distribution sector. With rising demand and ambitious decarbonisation targets across Ireland , this is an opportunity to contribute to critical infrastructure shaping the energy transition.
As an Electrical Engineer specialising in HV cable design, you’ll work on a diverse range of projects including HVDC interconnectors, offshore and onshore wind, substations, and grid connections—supporting initiatives aligned with EirGrid ’s network development.
You’ll collaborate within a multidisciplinary team across all project stages, from FEED to delivery, contributing technical expertise while developing your career in a supportive, innovation-driven environment.
About The Role
You will take on a key role within our growing Energy team, supporting the design and delivery of high-voltage cable systems across a range of major infrastructure and renewable energy projects throughout Ireland .
Working as part of a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment, you will contribute to projects spanning HVDC interconnectors, offshore and onshore wind farms, substations, and grid connection schemes. Your responsibilities will include supporting and leading design activities across all project phases—from feasibility and FEED through to detailed design and delivery—ensuring high-quality, efficient, and innovative engineering solutions.
You will work closely with internal teams and external stakeholders, including key clients such as EirGrid , helping to address complex technical challenges and deliver infrastructure that underpins Ireland’s transition to a more sustainable energy future.
This role offers the opportunity to apply your technical expertise, mentor junior engineers, and play an active part in shaping impactful projects, while continuing to develop your career within a supportive and forward-looking organisation.
YOUR IMPACT
In this role, you will help deliver safe, reliable and sustainable water infrastructure for communities across Ireland. Through your expertise in process design, you will develop effective treatment solutions that improve water quality and support resilient systems for the future.
You will assist in the mentorship and training of junior staff throughout there early career stages with Stantec.
Working closely with multidisciplinary teams and clients, you will contribute to innovative, practical solutions across the full project lifecycle. Your work will help ensure designs are efficient, compliant and deliver long-term value while supporting the collaborative culture that defines our team at Stantec.

You are a proactive and technically capable Electrical Engineer with a strong understanding of the electricity transmission and distribution sector.
You will ideally hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering (or a related field) from an accredited institution, with membership of Institution of Civil Engineers (EI) is preferred. You bring experience in civil substation engineering and a broad awareness of HV civil engineering projects.
You have hands-on experience in the design of transmission and distribution systems across all stages (Concept, FEED, and Detail Design), applying international standards for utility clients. Cable installation design, including routing layouts, trench/trenchless sections, bonding and phasing, pulling, termination, and jointing arrangements.
Proficiency with CYMCAP software for cable sizing calculations to international standards.
Strong computer literacy in MS Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook) and design tools such as AutoCAD or MicroStation.
You are adaptable and capable of managing challenging workloads under changing priorities, delivering high-quality results in a dynamic environment.

We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025.

We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment to assist with the growth of your career.

Great Benefits: Competitive salary, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard!

Based in Dublin, Galway, Castlebar and Cork, we are actively recruiting for team players with experience in any of the following areas – water and wastewater treatment process and network design, integrated network management, structural design, site development, road and bridge engineering, project management and administration.

jobs.title: Senior Instrumentation Technician – Water & Wastewater
jobs.desc:
Process Instrumentation | Chlorine | Turbidity | pH | DO | Flow | Level | Calibration | Commissioning
Water & Wastewater | €60,000–€70,000 DOE + Company Vehicle + Pension (39 hours per week)
RIGHT. Group, Castleisland, Co. Kerry | Kerry & Munster | Permanent
Are you an Instrument Technician who knows water and wastewater instrumentation?
We're looking for an experienced Water & Wastewater Instrumentation Technician who has hands-on experience calibrating, commissioning and fault-finding process instrumentation and analysers on water or wastewater treatment plants.
This isn't a general electrical role.
We're specifically looking for someone who understands the instruments that measure and control the water treatment process — and who is confident taking an instrument from installation, through calibration and commissioning, to a fully proven and documented system.
If your experience includes chlorine analysers, turbidity, pH, flow, level, pressure, temperature, dissolved oxygen and other process instrumentation, this could be the role for you.
What you'll actually be doing
You'll work directly on water and wastewater treatment infrastructure throughout Kerry and Munster, responsible for the installation, calibration, commissioning and fault-finding of process instrumentation.
Your work will include:
Process Instrumentation
Chlorine / residual chlorine analysers
pH analysers
Turbidity analysers
Dissolved oxygen
Conductivity
Suspended solids
Ammonia
Flow measurement
Level measurement
Pressure
Temperature
You'll be expected to understand not just how to wire an instrument, but what the instrument is measuring, how it should be calibrated and how the measurement relates to the treatment process.
Calibration & Commissioning
Carry out routine and commissioning calibration of process instruments.
Configure instrument ranges, scaling and outputs.
Verify 4–20 mA, digital and communication signals.
Perform loop checks from field instrument through to PLC/SCADA.
Carry out instrument verification and proving.
Investigate inaccurate, unstable or failed measurements.
Produce calibration certificates and commissioning records.
Diagnose instrument faults and determine whether the problem is the instrument, installation, cabling, process or control system.
Flow & Level
You'll have hands-on experience with technologies such as:
Electromagnetic flowmeters
Ultrasonic level
Radar level
Hydrostatic/submersible level
Pressure transmitters
Open-channel flow measurement
Analytical Instrumentation
This is a particularly important part of the role.
We are looking for someone who has actually worked with process analysers, including their calibration, cleaning, verification and fault-finding.
Experience with manufacturers such as Hach, Endress+Hauser, ABB, Siemens, VEGA or similar would be advantageous.
This role is for you if...
You have spent several years working on:
Water Treatment Plants
Wastewater Treatment Plants
Pumping Stations
Process Plants
and you are comfortable walking onto a site and being responsible for the instrumentation.
You don't need to be a PLC programmer.
You do need to understand how a field instrument works, how to calibrate it, how to prove its signal and how to determine why the value on the SCADA screen doesn't match what's actually happening in the process.
What we're looking for;
Essential
5+ years' hands-on instrumentation experience
Direct water or wastewater experience
Proven experience calibrating process instrumentation
Hands-on experience with water/wastewater analysers
Experience with chlorine, turbidity, pH, dissolved oxygen, flow, level, pressure and temperature instrumentation
Strong understanding of 4–20 mA instrumentation
Experience carrying out loop checks and commissioning
Ability to read P&IDs, loop drawings and instrument schedules
Experience fault-finding instrumentation connected to PLC/SCADA systems
Experience with VFDs would be advantageous
Full driving licence
Safe Pass
Particularly valuable experience
We're particularly interested in candidates who have worked with:
Chlorine analysers | Turbidity | pH | DO | Conductivity | Ammonia | Flowmeters | Radar/Ultrasonic Level | Pressure Transmitters
Why join Right Group?
This isn't a maintenance position where you'll be servicing the same equipment every day.
You'll work across a variety of water and wastewater projects, commissioning new equipment and working with experienced electrical, mechanical, process and automation engineers.
You'll get exposure to:
Instrumentation - Process - Electrical - PLC - SCADA - Automation- Commissioning
And as Right Group continues to grow, there is a genuine opportunity to progress into:
Senior Instrument Technician - Commissioning Lead- Instrumentation/Automation Lead
Package
€60,000–€70,000+ depending on experience
Company vehicle
Pension
Permanent position
Full-time employment
Training and manufacturer-specific development
Long-term project pipeline
Career progression
Work predominantly across Kerry & Munster
We're looking for the person who knows this stuff
If you've spent the last few years calibrating chlorine analysers, checking turbidity, calibrating pH, proving flowmeters, commissioning level instruments and fault-finding instrumentation on water or wastewater plants, we want to talk to you.
If that's you, apply to Right Group.

jobs.title: Control & Protection Engineer
jobs.desc:
Control & Protection Engineer (Cork)
Position Summary
NeoDyne are recruiting a
Control & Protection Engineer
to join our expanding Transmission & Distribution team. The successful candidate will support the design, configuration, and commissioning of protection and control systems for substations, renewable energy projects, and industrial power systems. Prior experience in these areas is highly desirable but not essential as we will provide all training.
The role is offered as a full-time staff position, based at our
Cork Office
, with an excellent Salary and Benefits package. If successful, you will enjoy NeoDyne's "People First" company culture, built on mutual respect, trust, and honesty, where each individual actively contributes as a valued team member.
Company Overview
NeoDyne is a leading engineering company specialising in industrial automation, digital manufacturing, and electrical engineering solutions. We develop high-availability automation and electrical systems for mission-critical industries, including pharmaceutical manufacturing, data centres, and energy infrastructure, ensuring continuous operation and compliance. Our expertise extend across power generation, natural gas transmission, and high-voltage system design, delivering robust solutions that strengthen critical infrastructure.
Within our
Transmission & Distribution
team, we deliver mission-critical design packages that transform the reliability, availability, and efficiency of the energy network, moving it towards a greener, more sustainable future. Department highlights include:
Driving complex design delivery: We design AIS/GIS substations from 20kV to 220kV and contestable build and non-contestable stations in the range of 40 to 550MVA CCGT. Connections include conventional and renewable Power Generation, Peaking, Battery Storage, DS3 and Solar PV plants and large demand loads such as data centres and process plants.
Delivery of high-complexity design frameworks: NeoDyne is a gas network design framework supplier, playing a significant role in providing electrical and instrumentation engineering services for the on-shore Natural Gas Industry and Regulated gas utility sector in Ireland and the UK. Our expertise include Compressor Station, AGI Electrical & Instrumentation design, Fiscal and non-Fiscal metering, and Cathodic Protection.
With a team of 220+ skilled engineers, our expertise spans the entire project lifecycle, from design and implementation to commissioning and operations. From our offices in Ireland, the UK, Romania, and the US, we operate on a global scale, combining technical expertise with local delivery. We support customers across Europe, North America, and Asia, delivering tailored engineering services that drive long-term success.
Key Responsibilities
Design and Engineering
Develop Protection and Control (P&C) designs for HV and MV substations, including protection schemes, control schematics, SLDs, and interlocking diagrams.
Specify and design AC/DC auxiliary systems, control panels, marshalling cabinets, and wiring diagrams.
Prepare Protection Coordination Studies, fault current calculations, and relay grading reports.
Select and configure protection relays and prepare detailed relay setting files.
Design and implement substation automation systems (SAS), RTU/PLC logic, and IEC 61850-based systems.
Create detailed control logic diagrams, signal lists, and communication interfaces for SCADA, RTU, and IED integration.
Testing, Commissioning, and Verification
Develop Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) and Site Acceptance Test (SAT) procedures for control and protection systems.
Carry out relay testing, secondary injection, and end-to-end testing.
Verify correct protection functionality, trip logic, interlocking, and communication protocols.
Provide on-site technical support during commissioning, energisation, and fault-finding phases.
Documentation and Compliance
Produce comprehensive design documentation, wiring schedules, technical specifications, and as-built drawings.
Ensure compliance with EirGrid, ESB Networks, and IEC/EN standards, as well as client-specific design rules.
Support the development and continuous improvement of design templates, engineering standards, and QA processes.
Project Delivery and Collaboration
Reporting to the Lead or Senior Engineering Manager on projects
Providing guidance and training to junior and graduate engineers.
Engage with clients, OEMs, and suppliers to clarify design interfaces, technical requirements, and delivery schedules.
Support proposal development, cost estimation, and technical tender reviews for new projects.
Experience & Skills
Required
Level 8 Degree in Electrical, Energy Engineering, or equivalent
4+ years' experience in a similar electrical or substation design role
Experience in developing Electrical Schematics using EPLAN.
Desired
Knowledge and experience in the Energy sector
Knowledge of Excel for calculations.
Characteristics
We look for candidates who
Work well as part of a team.
Have excellent problem solving and diagnostic skills.
Can complete tasks independently, capable of self-learning.
Can prioritise and coordinate work.
Have excellent customer service, interpersonal, communication and organisational skills.
Can multitask and work well under pressure.
Are a strategic business thinker.
What's on offer?
An opportunity to expand your knowledge beyond control & protection through company training, for example: Earth Grid Design, Reactive Power, Load Flow & Short Circuit Analysis, Substation Layouts Design, HV & MV Equipment Sizing and verification.
Competitive starting salary with year-on-year bonuses and salary increases.
Paid Overtime
PRSA pension with employer contribution
Health Insurance
Income Protection
Life Assurance
Flexible Working
Apply Now
Don't miss this opportunity to join a company at the forefront of industrial automation projects in Ireland, the UK, mainland Europe and the US. Apply now!
NeoDyne Ltd is an equal opportunity employer, and all applications will be treated in strictest confidence.

Tesco has operated in the Irish retail market since 1997, and with 190+ stores nationwide, we employ over 13,000 people in cities and towns around Ireland, supporting almost 45,000 jobs directly and indirectly. We partner with over 500 Irish suppliers - of which almost three-quarters are small and medium enterprises - which in turn supports almost 13,000 farming families around Ireland. Tesco is the single largest buyer of Irish food and drink in the world, buying €1.6 Billion a year; more than any other single country in the European Union, more than even the USA which you perceive as a massive buyer of Irish food.
We work closely with suppliers across Ireland who are dedicated to making the best products for our customers and this is reflected in the numerous awards our products have won over the years including Blás Na hÉireann, World Steak Challenge and Great Taste Awards.
We are proud to have an inclusive culture at Tesco where everyone truly feels able to be themselves. It is embedded in our values: we treat people how they want to be treated. So, talk to us throughout your application about how we can support.

You'll take ownership of delivering high-quality ecological assessments and technical reports, including Ecological Impact Assessments (EcIA), Preliminary Ecological Appraisals (PEA), Appropriate Assessment Screening, Natura Impact Statements (NIS) and EIAR chapters. Your expertise will also support project scoping, programme management, tender submissions and fee proposals, while representing Stantec at stakeholder meetings and oral hearings where required. Through your leadership, you'll help ensure our projects deliver positive environmental outcomes, champion biodiversity and sustainability, and continue to strengthen Stantec's reputation for technical excellence across Ireland.
About You
You'll be an experienced ecology professional with a passion for delivering high-quality environmental outcomes and developing the next generation of ecologists.
You'll Also Have
A degree in Ecology, Environmental Science or a related discipline.
Strong knowledge of Irish ecological legislation, planning processes and relevant European environmental directives and case law.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex ecological assessments across a range of infrastructure and development projects.
Experience participating in oral hearings.
Full Membership of CIEEM.
Chartered Ecologist
Excellent communication, report writing and stakeholder management skills.
The ability to manage multiple projects while leading multidisciplinary collaboration
WHY JOIN US
We put people first: We're proud of our friendly, inclusive and collaborative environment where everyone feels valued and driven to succeed.
We are driven to achieve: Named in the top 50 companies to work by Glassdoor 2025. Recognised by Corporate Knights as one of the world's top 10 most sustainable companies 2025.

We are better together: A supportive and collaborative team environment to assist with the growth of your career
Growth: We're on an exciting growth journey across the Ireland - we want you to be part of it!
Great Benefits: Competitive salary, enhanced pension plan, annual leave with the option to buy/sell additional days, private medical insurance, group income protection & life assurance included as standard!
About Stantec
Whether you’re starting out on your engineering career or are looking for a fresh challenge, Ryan Hanley, now part of Stantec, is a great career move.
Based in Dublin, Galway, Castlebar and Cork, we are actively recruiting for team players with experience in any of the following areas – water and wastewater treatment process and network design, integrated network management, structural design, site development, road and bridge engineering, project management and administration.
You’ll be working for a dynamic company with an excellent reputation in the industry.

jobs.title: Strategic Communications Graduate
jobs.desc:
See it differently
You see the world through a unique lens and that’s exactly what we need. We embrace how you see things differently – it’s essential for creating a sustainable future.
Arup is a global consultancy with advisory and technical expertise across more than 150 disciplines. We guide, plan and design the future of the built environment. Globally, each year we recruit hundreds of graduates and students who help us see things differently and solve the most complex challenges facing our clients, climate and communities.
The Opportunity
This role will be part of the Strategic Communications discipline, within the Strategy Consulting team. The team supports clients in navigating complex challenges, identifying opportunities, and executing sustainable transformational initiatives to achieve strategic communication and engagement objectives.
In this role, you will build experience in designing communication strategies, implementing and facilitating engagement programmes, and translating engagement insights into meaningful and impactful communications for stakeholders and clients. While the role centres on communications advisory and implementation, you will have the opportunity to collaborate with colleagues across the wider Strategy Consulting team, gaining exposure to diverse projects and perspectives.
As a Strategic Communications Graduate in our team at Arup, you will:
Support the development and delivery of communication and engagement strategies.
Create clear, audience-focused content across digital and multimedia channels.
Plan and support delivery of consultations, workshops, campaigns and stakeholder engagement activities.
Analyse engagement insights and help prepare reports, presentations and recommendations.
Coordinate project activities and build strong relationships with clients and colleagues.
https://www.arup.com/services/advisory-services/
Is this role right for you?
For this opportunity, we are seeking the following qualifications, skills and attributes:
An Undergraduate Or Bachelor's Degree (or Equivalent) In
Marketing; Strategic Communications, Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Marketing, Digital Marketing, Business, Commerce, Politics, Government, Public Policy, Sociology, Social Studies, Climate and Sustainability Science, Project and Programme Management, Change Management, Management, Management Consulting, Strategic Planning, or a related discipline.
Desired Technical Skills:
Microsoft 365 applications (Teams, Outlook, SharePoint, Word, PowerPoint, Excel and Forms). Adobe Creative Cloud, Canva, Miro and Power BI (desired).
Desired Key Competencies:
Excellent written and verbal communication, stakeholder engagement and mapping, workshop facilitation, social media and digital communications, strategic thinking, strong organisational skills, contextual awareness and a naturally curious mindset.
To Be Considered For a Graduate Opportunity, Your Application Must Include a Copy Of Your Academic Transcript And Meet The Following Criteria
Full working rights in the country of application
No more than 12 months of full-time experience in a comparable role
Recently graduated, or on track to graduate, from your most recent degree, related to your role of choice, before employment starts.
Alongside your degree, we look for the following core attributes;
Changemakers: A passion for sustainable development and creating a better world is key.
Innovative minds: We’re looking for critical thinkers who embrace new ideas and challenge the status quo.
Growth seekers: You have a growth mindset, always eager to learn and explore new ways of working.
Adaptable adventurers: You’re ready to take on any challenge that comes your way.
Closing Date:
12 November 2026
Please note, in the event of high applicant volume, this role may be closed ahead of the advertised closing date. We encourage you to apply early.
Eligibility
We're able to consider candidates who require an employment permit to work in Ireland, where the role and offered salary meet the Irish Government's eligibility criteria (for example, under the Critical Skills or General Employment Permit schemes). All Employment Permits are granted at the discretion of the Deciding Officer with offers contingent to obtaining the correct immigration to work and reside in Ireland.
What we offer you
At Arup, we care about each member’s success, so we can grow together.
Guided by our values, we provide an attractive total reward package that recognises the contribution of each of our members to our shared success. As well as competitive, fair and equitable pay, we offer a career in which all of our members can belong, grow and thrive – through benefits that support health and wellbeing, a wide range of learning opportunities and many possibilities to have an impact through the work they do.
We are owned in trust on behalf of our members, giving us the freedom, with personal responsibility, to set our own direction and choose work that aligns with our purpose and adds to Arup’s legacy. Our members collaborate on ambitious projects to deliver remarkable outcomes for our clients and communities. Profit Share is a key part of our reward, enabling permanent members to share in the results of our collective efforts.
We take an approach to flexible working that supports the diversity and wellbeing of our graduates.
Different people, shared values
Arup is an equal opportunity employer that actively promotes and nurtures a diverse and inclusive workforce. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds, regardless of age (within legal limits), gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, neurotype or mental health, race or ethnicity, faith or belief, sexual orientation, socioeconomic background, and whether you’re pregnant or on family leave. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas - this drives our excellence.
Guided by our values and alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, we create and contribute to equitable spaces and systems, while cultivating a sense of belonging for all. Our internal employee networks support our inclusive culture: from race, ethnicity and cross-cultural working to gender equity and LGBTQ+ and disability inclusion – we aim to create a space for you to express yourself and make a positive difference. Discover more about life at Arup at www.arup.com/careers/your-life-at-arup. We are an open environment that embraces diverse experiences, perspectives, and ideas.

Company Description
Work with Us. Change the World.
At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.
There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.
We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.
Job Description
Start here. Grow here.
Are you ready to join a team of talented engineers and shape the future of energy infrastructure? Join us and sit at the heart of our HV Substation Design team, leading design delivery on groundbreaking projects within a varied and exciting portfolio such as;
National Grid’s ‘Great Grid Upgrade’ Great Grid Partnership: Enabling the UK’s energy transition
Working with the world’s leading Hyperscalers and Data Centre Operators on forward-thinking, revolutionary projects.
EirGrid AECOM appointed to EirGrid engineering design, planning and project management services framework
Grow your career and apply your expertise within an innovative team of talented engineers!
Here’s what you’ll do:
Produce primary plant layouts for HV substations
Lead engineering design input to major infrastructure projects
Undertake Project Development/Pre-construction activities. E.g. the development of optimum cable routes considering length, thermal conditions and land use
Undertake equipment specifications for HV Plant and associated equipment
Develop specifications with technology specific specialists and external project partners
Develop tender specifications and undertake tender evaluations
Provide design assurance of tender return documentation, during tender evaluation and supplier meetings
At construction phase, review supplier technical designs, undertaking manufacturing assurance audits, attending FAT and providing commissioning support and fault resolution support
Be a trusted partner to key clients
Offer mentorship and guidance to junior team members
Driving excellence.
At AECOM, we are dedicated to fostering a culture of
innovation
and
collaboration
within our Transmission and Distribution team. We believe that technology should empower you so that you can focus on creative problem-solving, successfully manage complexity and deliver exceptional results. By embracing advanced automation tools, we seek imaginative thinkers who are excited about leveraging these tools to drive efficiency and enhance our projects. Join us in shaping the future of infrastructure, where your unique insights and creativity will play a vital role in our success!
Enjoy the Perks.
At AECOM, you'll enjoy a range of core and personalised benefits designed to support your future and well-being, customised to fit your lifestyle. Take advantage of career development opportunities, our flexible hybrid working model to ensure a work-life balance that suits your lifestyle, technical practice networks, AECOM University, and volunteering days.
Qualifications
Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?
Here’s what we’re looking for:
Degree in Electrical Engineering
Previous experience with consultancy, contractor or utility in the energy sector
Client experience with National Grid, ESB, EirGrid, SHET, SSE, SPT or any other transmission utility or developer in UK or Ireland
Extensive experience as FEED designer, detailed design or owner’s engineer role
Experience designing the HV infrastructure at concept and FEED design stages
Experience in detailed design, design assurance and owners engineer would be advantageous
Understanding of electrical AC HV Plant infrastructure and equipment both AIS and GIS
Good team player and have a client-focused mindset customer facing skills
Ability to work flexibly across multiple projects
Full driver licence
Ideally project management experience (incl. budget, time and quality)
Experience of managing multi-discipline engineering projects
We celebrate diversity, including neurodiversity, and believe it enriches our team. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and abilities. If you are an applicant with a disability that requires reasonable accommodation to complete the application process, please contact us at ReasonableAccommodations@aecom.com. At AECOM, we value everyone's unique contributions and perspectives.
If you meet some of the requirements above or have transferable skills you believe would benefit us, we would be delighted to hear from you!
Additional Information
Interested in the role or curious about life at AECOM? Follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube to explore our AECOM voices, employee stories, latest projects, and much more!
At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously.
To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.
About AECOM
AECOM is the world’s trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. On projects spanning transportation, buildings, water, new energy and the environment, our public- and private-sector clients trust us to solve their most complex challenges. Our teams are driven by a common purpose to deliver a better world through our unrivaled technical and digital expertise, a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion, and a commitment to environmental, social and governance priorities. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm and its Professional Services business had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. See how we are delivering sustainable legacies for generations to come at aecom.com and @AECOM.
Freedom to Grow in a World of Opportunity
You will have the flexibility you need to do your best work with hybrid work options. Whether you’re working from an AECOM office, remote location or at a client site, you will be working in a dynamic environment where your integrity, entrepreneurial spirit and pioneering mindset are championed.
You will help us foster a safe and respectful workplace, where we invite everyone to bring their whole selves to work using their unique talents, backgrounds and expertise to create transformational outcomes for our clients.
AECOM provides a wide array of compensation, benefits and well-being programs to meet the diverse needs of our employees and their families. We’re the world’s trusted global infrastructure firm, and we’re in this together – your growth and success are ours too.
Join us, and you’ll get all the benefits of being a part of a global, publicly traded firm – access to industry-leading technology and thinking and transformational work with big impact and work flexibility. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in each person’s potential, and we’ll help you reach yours.

jobs.desc:
​​​​ ​​​​​Senior Buyer
A well-established Irish engineering and manufacturing business specialising in bespoke construction and industrial solutions is expanding its procurement team and is looking for an experienced Senior Buyer to join the business.
This is a hands-on Senior Buyer role with ownership of key categories, supplier relationships and project procurement schedules. You'll work closely with Engineering, Production, Quality and Management to ensure materials and components are sourced competitively and delivered on time and on budget.
Responsibilities:
Manage day-to-day sourcing, purchasing and supplier follow-up across assigned categories, acting as the key procurement contact for projects.
Run RFQs/RFPs, compare supplier quotations and negotiate pricing, lead times and commercial terms.
Develop and maintain procurement schedules for major projects, tracking orders, deliveries and potential supply risks.
Build and manage supplier relationships, including performance tracking, onboarding, reviews and corrective actions.
Support cost-saving initiatives, new product launches and the identification of new suppliers and markets.
