jobs.title: Senior Financial Accountant
jobs.desc:
Contract: Permanent
Location: Cork
Join Musgrave – A Legacy of Innovation, Community, and Excellence
Musgrave is one of Europe’s most successful family-owned businesses, with a rich 150-year legacy in food and brand innovation. We're proud to serve communities across Ireland and Spain, feeding one in three people every day through 19 iconic brands like SuperValu, Centra, Mace, Frank and Honest, and Musgrave MarketPlace. By supporting thousands of retail and foodservice family businesses, we make a positive impact on the communities they serve. We're committed to becoming the most trusted and sustainable business in Ireland, and we're looking for dynamic, forward-thinking individuals to join us on this journey.
As we continue our journey toward becoming Ireland’s most trusted and sustainable business, we have an exciting opportunity for a successful candidate to join our Financal Control team.
Role Purpose
The Senior Financial Accountant – Northern Ireland is a senior Financial Control role responsible for the financial accounting, control, compliance and reporting agenda supporting the Musgrave Northern Ireland business.
The role owns cashflow forecasting, capital expenditure and depreciation reporting, quarterly HMRC compliance, intercompany governance in an outsourced operating model, and control and assurance reporting including MACSAC.
Working closely with NI Finance, Group Financial Control, Tax, Treasury, the outsourced service provider and External Audit, the role provides accurate reporting, independent challenge and assurance over the NI control environment, while driving standardisation and continuous improvement in line with the Group Financial Control agenda.
What you'll be doing:
Cashflow, Capital Expenditure & Depreciation
Own the preparation, review and challenge of short and medium-term cashflow forecasting for the NI business, including variance analysis against actuals. Including working capital reviews.
Forecast and report capital expenditure and the associated depreciation profile, working with business owners to validate phasing, spend and asset readiness.
Ensure capital spend is appropriately authorised, correctly capitalised and depreciated in line with Group accounting policy.
Provide insight to NI and Group leadership on cash, capex and depreciation trends, risks and opportunities.
Tax & Statutory Compliance (HMRC)
Prepare, review and submit quarterly HMRC returns for the NI entities, ensuring accuracy, completeness and timely filing.
Coordinate the quarterly VAT product file review process, engaging commercial and master data stakeholders to confirm correct VAT treatment and resolve exceptions.
Maintain robust documentation and audit trail supporting all returns and product file decisions.
Work with the Group Tax team on technical queries, legislative change and HMRC correspondence.
Intercompany Oversight & Outsourced Model Governance
Provide oversight and governance of intercompany transactions, balances, reconciliations and settlement across NI and Group entities.
Act as the retained control owner over activities performed by the outsourced service provider, reviewing outputs rather than performing the underlying processing.
Monitor service performance, SLA delivery and escalations, ensuring issues are resolved and root causes addressed.
Ensure intercompany balances are agreed, eliminated correctly on consolidation and supported by clear documentation.
Controls, Assurance & Reporting
Own MACSAC reporting for the NI business, including self-assessment, evidence, scoring and remediation of control gaps.
Ensure period-end controls, balance sheet reconciliations and journals meet Group standards and are reviewed on a timely basis.
Support internal and external audit requests and ensure timely closure of audit and management actions.
Prepare clear control and financial reporting updates for Financial Control forums and senior leadership.
Additional Financial Accounting Activity
Support the acquisition agenda within Retail.
Support lease accounting, including new leases, modifications and related disclosures.
Support insurance accounting, renewals data and related cost allocation.
Review employee expenses for compliance with policy, VAT treatment and control standards.
Support statutory financial statements preparation and audit for the NI entities.
Support wider Group Financial Control, transformation and process improvement initiatives as required.
What we are looking for:
Essential
Qualified Chartered Accountant (or equivalent).
3+ years post-qualified experience in financial accounting, financial control or audit.
Strong technical accounting knowledge and understanding of internal controls and financial governance.
Experience of cashflow forecasting, fixed assets and capital expenditure reporting.
Practical VAT and indirect tax compliance experience, ideally including HMRC filings.
Strong analytical, reconciliation and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.
Ability to work with and challenge an outsourced service provider in a retained oversight model.
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills across finance and non-finance audiences.
Desirable
Experience in retail, wholesale or FMCG.
Knowledge of UK and Irish tax and statutory reporting requirements.
Experience with Oracle, Onspring, Power BI or similar finance and control systems.
Why Musgrave:
Career Development: With a commitment to your personal and professional growth, Musgrave offers numerous opportunities for advancement and learning.
Collaborative Environment: Work alongside a passionate team, where your contributions will make a significant impact
Innovation Focus: Be part of a company that values forward-thinking solutions
Community Focus: Be part of a company that truly values its communities and strives to make a positive impact.
Be Part of a Legacy: Join a company with a long-standing commitment to community and innovation.
Ready to make an impact?
Apply now and be part of a forward-thinking company that values your expertise and vision.
Musgrave is an equal opportunities employer. We encourage applications from diverse candidates. If we can make any accommodations to enable you to be the best version of yourself during the interview, please let us know.

jobs.title: Quality Manager
jobs.desc:
The opportunity
Join a growing, internationally focused manufacturing business where Quality has a genuine seat at the table.
This is a high-impact role within a flat structure, giving you the opportunity to have your voice heard, influence senior decision-making and shape the future of the Quality function.
Working across a business driven by science, innovation, sustainability and quality, you'll have real scope to improve systems, develop people and influence operational excellence as the organisation continues to expand globally.
Why join?
Flat, collaborative structure - your expertise and opinions will be valued.
Global market exposure within an expanding business.
Genuine opportunity to influence strategy and operational decisions.
Ownership of the Quality function, with scope to shape and develop the team.
Strong focus on innovation, sustainability and continuous improvement.
A role combining strategic influence with hands-on operational impact.
What you'll be responsible for
Lead the Quality function across manufacturing operations.
Own quality performance, product release, traceability and quality systems.
Ensure compliance with relevant legislation/customer standards.
Manage the Quality Management System, document control and audit programmes.
Lead regulatory, certification and customer audits.
Oversee analytical testing, HACCP-based risk assessment and verification programmes.
Manage supplier approval and raw material change control.
Lead customer complaints, non-conformances, root cause analysis and corrective actions.
Drive continuous improvement and operational excellence.
Develop the Quality team through effective training and capability building.
Work cross-functionally with Operations, Commercial, Manufacturing and Senior Management.
What we're looking for
7+ years' experience in FMCG.
Previous Quality Manager experience within a production/processing environment.
Degree in a Science-related subject.
Level 5 HACCP qualification or higher.
Strong knowledge of Food Safety & Quality Management Systems.
Strong understanding of food/feed legislation, customer standards and Codes of Practice.
Experience with auditing, ideally Lead Auditor/Internal Auditor training.
Strong leadership and people-management skills.
Confident communicating with customers, suppliers and senior management.
Excellent problem-solving, organisational and interpersonal skills.

jobs.title: Cleaner
jobs.desc:
Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work with the biggest companies in the world to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.
The Eurofins network is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across its companies around the world.
We’re proud to be an armed forces-friendly place to work and welcome applications from reservists, armed forces veterans (including the wounded, injured and sick), as well as cadet instructors, and military spouses and partners.
If you want to continue to help make our world a safer and healthier place, then apply for the role below and become a part of the extraordinary Eurofins network
Job Description
This role will be working within a Food Testing laboratory to ensure the premises is kept in a clean and tidy manner.
This is a full time role working 39 hours per week - Monday 09:30-18:00 and Tuesday to Friday 10:45 - 19:00.
Responsible for the collection and disposal of general waste, recycling, cardboard and food waste from all designated laboratory areas in accordance with company procedures and safety requirements.
Responsible for ensuring waste streams are segregated correctly and disposed of in compliance with quality, environmental and health and safety requirements.
Responsible for the cleaning, washing, sanitising and storage of laboratory consumables, including glassware, containers and other reusable laboratory items.
Responsible for maintaining high standards of housekeeping throughout all laboratory areas, ensuring workspaces, corridors, storage areas and communal areas are clean, tidy and safe at all times.
Responsible for identifying and reporting housekeeping, maintenance or safety concerns.
Qualifications
Experience in industrial cleaning is preferable.
Experience in a cleaning role.
Able to work as part of a team.
Good communications skills.
Additional Information
As a Eurofins employee you will benefit from:
On successful completion of probation – Healthcare will be covered by company.
Pension contribution on commencement of employment – 2% [employer / employee contribution] and once probation is passed employee can increase contribution to 5% [er/ee]
Discretionary Annual Performance related bonus, based on employee and company performance.
Annual leave days 22 days.
Service days accrued based on service
Life Assurance from Day one of employment
Educational assistance policy
Income Protection

Our people are the backbone of what we do, so it's incredibly important we find the right individuals to join us. As a potential new recruit you'll be invited to meet the team in the form of an assessment centre or a staged interview process dependent on the role and it's requirements, this will give you the opportunity to see what working for Eurofins is really like and enable us to get you know your key skills and strengths.

As part of any recruitment process, the company collects and processes personal data relating to job applicants. The company is committed to being transparent about how it collects and uses that data and to meeting its data protection obligations.

jobs.desc:
As a Section 39 organisation, KPFA operates its own pay scales.
Annual increments are awarded up to the maximum point of the relevant scale.
WE ARE CURRENTLY RECRUITING FOR THE FOLLOWING POSITION
Post: Cook
Contract: Specified Purpose, Part-Time (14 hours per week) Maternity Leave Cover
Location: Tearmann Lodge, Rathmore
Roster: Week 1:
Sat, Sun, Thurs and Fri: 10:00 am–2:00 pm
Week 2:
Mon, Tues and Wed: 10:00 am–2:00 pm
Rosters may be subject to change due to the operational requirements of the service*
The Cook is an integral part of the on-duty team and flexibility is essential for the role as priorities and duties can change to meet the needs of residents. As a key team player, they will be responsible for the delivery of well balanced and nourishing meals and snacks to all residents and for ensuring the efficient operation of his/her function within a set budget.
The Role:
Responsible for the provision of good quality, home cooked food at all times.
Ensure that meals are prepared at the agreed times and at correct temperatures.
Responsible for the ordering of all ingredients in quantities, which are economically sound.
Ensure that food is stored appropriately at all times.
Maintain a high level of service and hygiene within the kitchen
Ensure that the kitchen area, stores and dining room are maintained in a clean condition at all times.
Compile seasonal menus, giving consideration to special diets, likes and dislikes of residents with the approval of the centre manager.
Supervise and instruct staff as necessary in the preparation of food and on safety within the kitchen.
Observe good health and safety practices at all times, thus ensuring the safety of residents, staff and members of the public.
Understand and follow the regulations required by the Environmental Health Department when preparing food.
Responsible for the daily management and supervision of the kitchen.
Essential Criteria
Be able to carry out the duties of the post satisfactorily.
Have a good working knowledge of relevant legislation and standards, including Health and Safety, Infection Prevention and Control, and HACCP.
Hold valid HACCP certification.
Demonstrate a commitment to providing a high quality service.
Have the ability to work effectively as part of a team and build positive working relationships.
Applicants should have the necessary authorisation to work in Ireland and will be asked to provide supporting documentation during the recruitment process.
Highly desirble criteria
A recognised qualification in Professional Cookery, Culinary Arts, Catering, Food Production or a related area.
Previous experience in a Cook, Chef, Catering Assistant or similar food preparation role.
Experience preparing meals for people with specific dietary requirements, including modified diets, allergies and special dietary needs.
Experience working in a healthcare, disability, residential or community setting.
Experience in menu planning, portion control and preparing nutritious, well-balanced meals.
A good understanding of dignity, choice and individual preferences when providing meals to people using disability services.
Hold a full driver’s licence, have proven driving experience, and be willing to drive Association vehicles. Regarding use of own vehicle for work purposes, applicants must ensure it is roadworthy and covered by valid business insurance (or be willing to obtain business use insurance).
Employee Benefits: Sick Pay Scheme, Paid Maternity Leave, Flexible Working, Employee Assistance Programme, Pension Scheme, Parking ( Site Dependent), Generous Annual Leave, Access to income continuance scheme, Discounted Health Insurance and Access to training.

Failure to provide this information, along with a satisfactorily completed verification of service form before an agreed start date, will result in placement at Point 1 of the applicable scale. Incremental credit will only be applied from the date correct documents are submitted.*
Your CV must be written independently and accurately reflecting your own experience, skills, and competencies. The use of AI or automated tools to complete any part is not permitted.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Graduate Programme 2026
jobs.desc:
Interested in smart manufacturing? Want to influence the power grid of the future? Tackle climate change? Launch your career with NeoDyne and open a world of opportunities!
Overview
NeoDyne is a leading engineering company specialising in industrial automation, digital manufacturing, and electrical engineering solutions. With a strong presence across multiple sectors, including Life Sciences, Food & Beverage, and Energy, NeoDyne delivers leading-edge solutions that drive efficiency, safety, and performance for its customers worldwide.
We develop high-availability automation and electrical systems for mission-critical industries, including pharmaceutical manufacturing, data centres, and energy infrastructure, ensuring continuous operation and compliance. We additionally integrate emerging technologies to enhance control, scalability, and operational insight. Our expertise also extends to power generation, natural gas transmission, and high-voltage system design, delivering robust solutions that strengthen critical infrastructure.
With a team of 200+ skilled engineers, our expertise spans the entire project lifecycle, from design and implementation to commissioning and operations. From our offices in Ireland, the UK, Romania, and the US, we operate on a global scale, combining technical expertise with local delivery. We support customers across Europe, North America, and Asia, delivering tailored engineering services that drive long-term success.
Position Summary
NeoDyne are recruiting a
Graduate Mechanical Engineer
to join our expanding engineering teams. Our graduate programme is all about learning new and developing your existing skills. Over a two-year period, you will be placed in projects where you get to do meaningful work and contribute to the business.
This Graduate opportunity is offered as a full-time permanent contract, based at our
Cork Office
, with an excellent salary and benefits package. If successful, you will enjoy NeoDyne's "People First" company culture, built on mutual respect, trust, and honesty, where each individual actively contributes as a valued team member.
What might I be doing?
Mechanical Design: Support the design of mechanical systems for industrial, manufacturing and critical infrastructure projects, including equipment layouts, piping and utility systems.
Equipment & Engineering: Assist with equipment selection and specification, and carry out mechanical calculations such as pipe sizing, pressure drops and pump sizing.
Drawings & Documentation: Develop and review mechanical drawings, P&IDs, equipment specifications, datasheets and technical documentation.
Multidisciplinary Projects: Work alongside mechanical, electrical, automation and instrumentation engineers to deliver coordinated engineering solutions.
Site & Commissioning: Visit customer sites to support surveys, installation, equipment inspections, testing and commissioning, gaining hands-on experience of bringing designs into operation.
What about training?
Our induction programme revolves around a 70-20-10 model for learning and development.
70% On-the-job Learning: You'll get stuck in from Day 1, working on real projects, delivering real business value to our customers both on- and off-site.
20% Learning from others: You'll be part of a team, working with subject matter experts and interacting with our customers daily. You'll receive support and guidance, and an invaluable opportunity to learn from former graduates who've seen it and done it.
10% Formal Education: We'll help you become an expert in your chosen field, backed up by formal e-learning and classroom training. This extends to attaining professional certifications where relevant to our business specialisations.
Required
Experience & skills
Level 8 Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical & Manufacturing Engineering, Energy Engineering, or equivalent.
0-2 years' experience in a similar mechanical design role or Work Placement.
Full Irish driving license or to be achieved within 12 months of starting the role.
Desired
A strong understanding of fundamental mechanical engineering principles.
Experience using mechanical design or CAD software such as AutoCAD, SolidWorks, Inventor, Revit or similar.
Characteristics
We look for candidates who
Work well as part of a team.
Have excellent problem solving and diagnostic skills.
Can complete tasks independently, capable of self-learning.
Can prioritise and coordinate work.
Have excellent customer service, interpersonal, communication and organisational skills.
Can multitask and work well under pressure.
Are a strategic business thinker.
What's on offer?
Competitive starting salary with year-on-year bonuses and salary increases
Paid Overtime
Paid Graduation Day
Health Insurance
Income Protection
Life Assurance
PRSA pension with employer contribution
Flexible Working
Personalised Career Development Plan
Professional Certifications, pathways to become a Chartered Engineer
Cycle to work scheme
Apply today!
With our diverse range of business specialisations, customers, and industries that we serve, we offer an unrivalled programme designed to accelerate your personal and professional development. Don't miss this opportunity to join a company at the forefront of industrial automation projects in Ireland, the UK, mainland Europe and the US.
So why wait? Apply Today!
NeoDyne Ltd. is an equal opportunity employer, and all applications will be treated in strictest confidence.

jobs.title: Intern
jobs.desc:
Own Every Moment at NetApp
At NetApp, your ideas power innovation. We lead in intelligent data infrastructure—delivering unified storage, integrated data services, and solutions that help organizations unlock the full potential of their data, from AI to multicloud.
Ready to innovate and contribute to our path to $10B? Here, you'll collaborate with passionate teams, tackle real-world challenges, and see your impact in how customers transform and grow. If you're ready to bring curiosity, creativity, and drive to every moment, NetApp is where your journey begins. Join teams that innovate to elevate, drive results, and excel together across every function.
About NetApp
The market has shifted. AI is accelerating. The key to AI success is intelligent data and the infrastructure to manage it. Customers are urgently rethinking how they modernize, secure, and unlock value from their data. NetApp is built for this exact moment — with a differentiated platform, deep enterprise credibility, and a clear strategy to win.
Joining NetApp now means operating in a high achievement environment where you are empowered to own every moment. Our culture is grounded in three principles: innovate to elevate, drive results, excel as a team. These are more than words. They define how we show up, how we sell, and how we grow.
Position Overview
As a  Sales Intern you'll gain hands-on experience supporting customer success and learning the fundamentals of modern sales. This internship is ideal for students passionate about building relationships, solving problems, and exploring how technology drives business transformation.  You’ll work with one of our dynamic specialist and hybrid  teams—such as Partner, Strategic, or Commercial Sales, Renewals, Go-to-Market Strategy, Sales Operations, or other areas—contributing to initiatives that strengthen our sales approach and help grow customer relationships. This role offers exposure to innovative sales practices, customer engagement strategies, and data-driven decision-making, all while being mentored by experienced professionals.
Key Responsibilities
Utilize strong interpersonal communication and customer service skills to work effectively with prospects, customers, and cross-functional teams to meet performance goals.
Quickly learn and adopt new sales technologies, CRM systems, and digital tools to support customer engagement activities.
Support the execution of core sales and business development activities while following established sales methodologies and processes.
Drive AI-driven solutions to enhance customer experience and optimize workflows.
Your Profile
Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Business, Sales, Communications, or a related field.
Familiarity with AI tools and technologies
Self-starter with a collaborative mindset and a willingness to learn in a fast-paced environment.
Creative approach to problem-solving.
You must have the unrestricted right to work in Ireland throughout the duration of the internship.
Available to come into the office three times per week as a part of NetApp’s hybrid work culture.
Start Date
: 4th January, 2027
At NetApp, we embrace a hybrid working environment designed to strengthen connection, collaboration, and culture for all employees. This means that most roles will have some level of in-office and/or in-person expectations, which will be shared during the recruitment process.
Equal Opportunity Employer:
NetApp is firmly committed to Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and to compliance with all federal, state and local laws that prohibit employment discrimination based on age, race, color, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, religion, disability or genetic information, pregnancy, protected veteran status, and any other protected classification.
Why You'll Thrive at NetApp
At NetApp, you won't wait for the perfect moment—you'll make it. The early planning, the extra thought, the bold idea that turns good into great: That's how our people operate and how we continue to push the boundaries of data infrastructure.
NetApp is the trusted partner for organizations transforming data into opportunity. As the only enterprise-grade storage service natively embedded in Google Cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure, we empower customers to run everything from traditional workloads to enterprise AI with unmatched performance, resilience, and security.
Our culture
We celebrate mold breakers, bold thinkers, and problem solvers. We reward initiative, impact, and ownership. We provide flexibility so you can balance professional ambition with your personal life. Here, differences are not just welcomed—they drive everything we do.
If you're ready to innovate, rise to the challenge, and own every moment - make your next move your best one. Apply now.
Submitting an Application
To ensure a streamlined and fair hiring process for all candidates, our team only reviews applications submitted through our company website. This practice allows us to track, assess, and respond to applicants efficiently. Emailing our employees, recruiters, or Human Resources personnel directly will not influence your application.
AI Disclosure
For select roles, some stages of our hiring process may use artificial intelligence tools to help evaluate applications and candidate selection. These tools support—rather than replace—human decision-making.

jobs.title: Commercial Sales & E-Commerce Executive
jobs.desc:
Talbot Hotel Cork, part of the Talbot Collection, are currently recruiting for
Commercial Sales & E-Commerce Executive
to join our team. The successful candidate will be a team player, be flexible and will be motivated by delivering exceptional customer service, must be available to work midweek & weekends.
The Talbot Collection are one of the
Best Places to Work in Hospitality 2026
as awarded by the Great Place to Work. Come experience it for yourself and join our team.
Job Purpose
To support and grow the hotel's commercial performance through accurate sales administration, website and e-commerce management, social media activity, digital campaigns and Meetings & Events coordination. The role helps convert enquiries into confirmed business, strengthen direct revenue and deliver a clear, consistent customer booking journey.
Key Responsibilities & KPIs
E-commerce, Website & Social Media
Maintain accurate, up-to-date website offers, packages, pricing, inclusions, availability, images, terms and booking links; coordinate changes with Sales & Marketing and Revenue.
Manage hotel social channels and a content calendar; create, schedule and publish relevant posts, stories, reels and promotional content for rooms, dining, weddings, events, leisure and seasonal offers.
Promote approved campaigns, gift vouchers and experiences; respond to or direct digital enquiries promptly and ensure messaging follows brand guidelines.
KPIs: timely and accurate updates; social reach and engagement; website traffic, digital enquiries, booking conversion and direct revenue where measurable.
Sales Administration & Commercial Reporting
Maintain CRM, sales databases and enquiry tracker; log enquiries, outcomes and follow-ups, prepare quotations, proposals, contracts and sales documentation, and follow up outstanding opportunities.
Produce accurate weekly/monthly sales, enquiry, conversion and pipeline reports; maintain confidentiality and comply with GDPR.
KPIs: enquiry response and follow-up times; CRM accuracy; quotation/document turnaround; report completion; enquiry-to-booking conversion and recorded lost-business reasons.
Meetings & Events Coordination
Support the Meetings & Events team with enquiry qualification, tailored proposals, quotations, contracts, confirmations, function details, rooming lists and event documentation.
Communicate requirements to operational departments, liaise with clients before events, support post-event follow-up and identify suitable upselling opportunities.
KPIs: timely proposals and follow-ups; enquiry conversion and confirmed event revenue; accuracy of event details; additional revenue from upgrades and add-ons; client feedback.
Digital Campaigns & Cross-Department Support
Support email and digital campaigns, seasonal promotions, local opportunities and sales collateral; ensure campaigns direct customers to the correct booking or enquiry channel.
Work collaboratively with Revenue, Reservations, Front Office, Food & Beverage, Leisure, Weddings and Group Commercial teams; escalate pricing, contractual or expenditure decisions requiring approval.
KPIs: campaign-generated enquiries/bookings and attributable revenue; campaign accuracy and deadlines; effective interdepartmental communication and completion of agreed actions.
Skills, Qualifications & Experience
Experience in hotel sales, sales administration, reservations, e-commerce, digital marketing or Meetings & Events; hospitality experience is desirable.
Excellent written and verbal communication, customer service and relationship-management skills, with strong organisation and attention to detail.
Confident using Microsoft Office, databases/CRM and digital platforms; website content, booking engines, social media scheduling, analytics and email marketing experience is desirable.
Commercially aware, proactive and adaptable, able to manage competing deadlines, interpret reports and work independently while contributing to a team.
Relevant qualification in Business, Hospitality, Sales, Marketing or Digital Marketing is desirable. Commitment to confidentiality, GDPR and hotel procedures is essential.
Role Summary
This is a commercially focused role combining e-commerce and social media management, sales administration, digital revenue support and Meetings & Events coordination. By keeping online offers accurate, managing enquiries and follow-ups, supporting event sales and tracking results, the Executive will help improve sales efficiency, customer experience and measurable revenue opportunities. The role operates within approved pricing, brand guidelines and procedures; new rates, discounts, significant campaign spend and non-standard commercial terms require management approval.
Benefits & Development with Talbot Collection
Role-specific training in hotel systems, CRM and enquiry tracking, website and booking processes, Meetings & Events procedures, commercial reporting, pricing approvals, GDPR and Talbot Collection standards.
Ongoing development of digital sales, e-commerce, reporting and commercial skills, with performance reviews and agreed objectives.
Opportunity to work collaboratively across hotel departments and the wider Talbot Collection, contributing ideas and supporting initiatives that improve guest experience and business performance.
A professional, supportive and collaborative working environment, with the opportunity to build hospitality and commercial experience.
Performance Review & General Responsibilities
Initial KPI baselines should be established during the first 60-90 days, with measurable targets agreed with the Sales & Marketing Manager and Revenue Manager based on enquiry volumes, historical performance, resources and available reporting systems. The Executive is expected to maintain accurate records, attend relevant meetings and training, follow company policies and procedures, protect confidential information, and undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the role.
Some of the benefits of joining the team:
One of the Best Places to Work in Hospitality 2026 as awarded by the Great Place Work
Join a company and culture that put their team first
Training and Development Opportunities we invest in our people
Being part of a progressive & growing company.
Contributory company pension scheme.
Company Life Insurance Scheme
Free parking
Staff meals
Employee Assistance Programme
Talbot Collection Friends and Family Rates on accommodation
Bike to Work
Christmas Savings Scheme
